note: Evidence for flag eras. An era is listed only once someone has read its sources; every other era is unreviewed. Only positive evidence is written here, and what could not be confirmed is said in `open`, not left out.

classes.attested: Sources show this flag in use in this period. Needs one primary or reference source, or two compiled sources from different publishers.
classes.reconstructed: Described in sources but no image survives; the drawing is a reconstruction.
classes.symbolic: An emblem, banner or standard shown for a polity that had no flag of its own.
classes.none: No flag evidence exists; the image is a placeholder.
classes.unreviewed: Not yet checked against sources. The page text is the original compilation.
classes.placeholder: The image is a placeholder, as the page's own caption says. Whether a flag existed was not checked.

kinds.primary: The decree, document, image or object itself, or a museum record of it.
kinds.reference: A scholarly or institutional account that names its basis.
kinds.compiled: A general compilation (Wikipedia, Flags of the World); useful, but a copy of other writers.

era-1945.says: A royal decree of 19 February 1937, no. 93, fixed the colours of the flag of the Kingdom as red, white and blue; FOTW and Wikipedia both quote it that way. The Royal House says the colours were bright vermilion and cobalt blue.
era-1945.open: The sources disagree on the shade: FOTW dates 'bright vermilion and cobalt blue' to 1958, while the Royal House page gives that wording as the decree's own. The decree text itself has not been read. The hex swatches on this page are approximations, not a specification.

era-1940.says: FOTW, citing Poels in Vexilla Nostra 198 (1995), says the tricolour stayed the national flag but its use was restricted by the occupiers. NOS reports that from 1940 any demonstrative act for the House of Orange was punishable.
era-1940.open: No ordinance was found, so which restrictions fell on the tricolour, and when, is not established. An earlier version of this page said it was 'banned outright in 1943'; no source for that was found and it was removed. The flag drawn is the occupier's, schematically.

era-1830.open: Not yet checked against a source. That the flag was unchanged through the 1830 secession is plausible but unsourced here.

era-1813.says: Wikipedia reports 1813 newspapers describing red-white-blue flags with orange pennants and solid orange flags, and says the question of the national flag was left undecided; its statement that William preferred red-white-blue is marked 'citation needed' there. The Royal House confirms independence returned in 1813 but says nothing about the flag.
era-1813.open: One secondary source for the flag question; not enough to call it attested.

era-1810.says: The Royal House says the Netherlands was annexed by France in 1810 and the national flag was replaced by the French imperial standard. Wikipedia says the national flag was replaced by imperial emblems in 1810, without a citation there.
era-1810.open: Which French flag flew on Dutch buildings is not established; 'imperial standard' may not be the plain tricolour drawn here. Wikipedia's own Kingdom of Holland page gives the annexation date inconsistently.

era-1806.says: The tricolour continued under Louis Bonaparte. Wikipedia dates the flag without the Maiden to 5 June 1806 (no citation there), records naval crews rioting over the flag in August 1806 and a royal decree of 1 December 1807 affirming the Statenvlag for the navy (both citing de Jonge, 1831). FOTW says Louis proposed adding quartered arms to the navy's flag and withdrew the proposal when the navy would not accept it.
era-1806.open: The 5 June 1806 date has no primary source behind it in either reference. The motive this page used to state ('a deliberate choice to present continuity') had no source and was removed.

era-1795.says: Dirk Langendijk's design in the Rijksmuseum shows the Dutch Maiden and the Lion holding a spear topped with a liberty cap, in the upper-left corner of the existing flag, for the Batavian navy, effective 1 March 1796. FOTW, citing Wilson (1986, p. 60), puts the decree altering the navy's flags (not the merchant flags) on 14 February 1796; the States General publication Wikipedia cites carries the same date.
era-1795.open: The emblem was on the navy's flag only. Its removal in 1806 is Wikipedia's, without a citation. FOTW also describes a tricolour 'with a small white canton' (credited to Roy Stilling, 1996), which we have not reconciled with the Maiden emblem. This page used to describe a 'canton with a liberty cap used briefly 1795-96'; that is not what the sources show.

era-1650.says: Red replaced orange gradually. Wikipedia places the transition between about 1630 and 1660, with red appearing as early as 1596-97 (its infobox and text differ), the name Statenvlag in 1664 (de Jonge, 1833, p. 75) and the navy always flying it after 1663 (de Waard, 1900). The Royal House says red gradually replaced orange during the 17th century because orange is less visible at sea. Wikipedia gives the Republic's distance from the House of Orange as the reason.
era-1650.open: No decree for the change was found, so 'c. 1650' is the midpoint of a transition, not an event. This page used to say the flag flew over the VOC and WIC fleets, New Amsterdam and Batavia; no source for that was found and it was removed.

era-1581.says: Orange-white-blue is attested from the 1570s. Wikipedia cites Rey (1837) for use by the Prince of Orange then, Jacob Duym for officers' brassards at the siege of Leiden in 1574, an order of the Admiralty of Zeeland of 1587 for naval flags in these colours, and de Waard (1900) for the navy flying it from 1588 to 1630. The Royal House dates the first reference to 1572; FOTW says it was used from the second half of the 16th century and named for William of Orange.
era-1581.open: Wikipedia calls it uncertain whether the Sea Beggars carried the colours at Den Briel in 1572, so this page no longer says it flew from the Sea Beggars onward. The era starts at the Act of Abjuration (1581), not at the flag's first appearance. The earliest colour image, of 1575 in Jan van Hout's album, is on Wikipedia without a reference we could read.

era-1433.says: The Cross of Burgundy was the emblem of the Burgundian dukes (Hutchinson, 2007, as cited on Wikipedia). It is drawn here as the emblem, not as a flag of the northern provinces.
era-1433.open: Its use as a flag across the Habsburg Netherlands after 1477 is stated on Wikipedia without a citation and has not been confirmed.

era-1000.says: No single polity existed, so there is no flag to attest; the maroon field is a placeholder.

era-50bce.says: Tacitus (Histories 4.22) describes the force under Civilis following images of wild beasts brought out of woods and sacred groves, and names the Batavian elite and 'German allies'. He describes no flag.
era-50bce.open: This page used to say Tacitus records Batavian and Frisian war-standards; the passage names the Batavians and unnamed German allies, not the Frisii.

era-15.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 27 October 1997; Flags of the World dates it 4 January 2004.
era-15.open: The two sources do not agree on a year with each other, or one is silent, so 2021, the year this page starts the current flag, could not be confirmed. Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-550bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — two millennia of successive outside empires».
era-550bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-2001.says: Both: a black-red-green tricolour with the national emblem, 2004. Wikipedia: restored 28 January 2002, 2004 version used from 9 October 2004 to 15 August 2021 (2013 latest version). FOTW: 4 January 2004 tricolour, 2:3, bearing 1298 AH.
era-2001.open: The mosque-and-wheat emblem content and the shahada placement on this page are not covered; the two sources differ on the 2004 day (4 January vs 9 October).

era-27.says: Wikipedia: plain white banner 27 Sep 1996 to 26 Oct 1997; black shahada on white 26 Oct 1997 to 13 Nov 2001.
era-27.open: FOTW's page covers only 2002 onward; a second publisher is missing. The symbolism claim is uncovered.

era-28.says: Wikipedia: provisional flag 27 Apr-6 Dec 1992 with a takbir stripe and white shahada stripe, red removed; Rabbani government flag with shahada and 1298 on the emblem 7 Dec 1992-27 Jan 2002 in Northern Alliance areas. FOTW: calls it the 1992-2002 flag, caption Dec 1992-Sep 1996 conflicting with its text, no colours.
era-28.open: Neither source states the colours as green-white-black; the drawing and the 'ancestor of 2004 flag' claim are uncovered.

era-27-1.says: Wikipedia: tricolour without seal 27 Apr-18 Oct 1978; red flag with yellow seal 19 Oct 1978-21 Apr 1980; tricolour restored 22 Apr 1980 to 29 Nov 1987.
era-27-1.open: FOTW does not cover 1978-80. Flags after 1987 to 1992 are not covered by the sources read.

era-17.says: Wikipedia: monarchy flag minus the year, 17 Jul 1973-8 May 1974; new seal with golden eagle, minbar, wheat and sun rays 9 May 1974-26 Apr 1978.

era-1919.says: Wikipedia: 1919 flag without tricolour (cannons removed, rays in an octagram); oval 1921; tricolour about June 1928, modelled on the German flag of that era; white seal added 1901.
era-1919.open: FOTW does not cover 1919-1973. The page's colour meanings and the 1919 tricolour claim are not supported.

era-1747.says: Wikipedia: black field attributed to the Hotak dynasty (early 18th century); last solid black flag under Abdur Rahman; Herat flag under Kamran Shah Durrani about 1818-1842 with no design given.
era-1747.open: FOTW does not cover this span. Durrani 1747-1818 designs are not described by the sources read.

era-1991.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 1443; Flags of the World dates it 7 April 1992.
era-1991.open: Both sources give 1992 for the current flag, which is after 1991, the year this page starts the era. Either the era begins under an earlier flag or one of the dates is wrong. Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1946.says: Wikipedia: in early 1946 a gold star was placed above the eagle; Law 5506 of 28 December 1976 describes a red five-pointed star embroidered in gold, designed by Sadik Kaceli. FOTW: in 1946 a red five-pointed star with gold border was placed above the eagle's heads. Both give removal on 7 April 1992.
era-1946.open: Page said the star went 'the moment the single-party state ended'; sources date removal to 1992.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia: a flag of the Democratic Government was published in War Bulletin no. 51 of 28 November 1944 and used at the Constitutional Assembly on 10 January 1946; it gives no star colour or border. FOTW: the partisan government in 1944 reintroduced the pre-war flag with a gold star near the hoist, later replaced by hammer and sickle.
era-1944.open: The page's red star outlined in black above the eagle is contradicted by FOTW (gold star near the hoist); the 1944 flag's exact form is not settled by the sources read.

era-1943.says: Wikipedia: in October 1943 the union with Italy was dissolved and pre-Italian flags and symbols were reused.
era-1943.open: FOTW describes no flag for the German occupation. The sources do not say whether the royal helmet was absent, as the page states.

era-1939.says: Wikipedia: a fascist flag replaced Zog's on 4 December 1939 (Pathe footage); the 1940 Yearbook describes the eagle with a lictor's fasces at the centre. FOTW: in 1939 the flag becomes plain red with new arms: red shield, black eagle, black helmet, two black fasces and the motto FERT on a scroll.
era-1939.open: The sources describe fasces as part of an arms or central device, not a small fasces added beneath the eagle; the two sources differ on layout and no image was seen.

era-1928.says: Wikipedia: the 1928 Fundamental Statute (art. III) describes a red flag with a black double-headed eagle; a crown was added in Zog's reign, in variants 1928-34 and 1934-39; the Skanderbeg helmet appears only in the 2014 presidential flag. FOTW: in 1928 the eagle was surmounted by Skanderbeg's helmet in gold as the royal crown.
era-1928.open: Sources disagree on crown versus helmet. The page's claim that the helmet device was 'later revived on the republic's coat of arms' is not supported; Wikipedia ties the helmet to the 2014 presidential flag.

era-1925.says: Wikipedia: the republic's flag was square, first shown in Teki Selenica's 1927 guide. FOTW: the First Republic (dated 1920 there) flew a plain black eagle on red.
era-1925.open: FOTW dates the republic's flag to 1920, not 1925; the sources read do not give an independent 1925 description beyond the square shape.

era-1914.says: Wikipedia: Essad Pasha's flag was light red with a white star polygon, like the Ottoman flag without crescent (letter of 7 May 1915); the Principality section (red, black eagle) is unsourced; a 1915 flag from Durres is in the Albanian National History Museum; Korce raised a flag on 10 December 1916; a surviving Lushnje-era flag (1920) is dark red with black eagle, 121 x 70 cm. FOTW: the 1914 principality flag had a golden beak, claws and arrows on the eagle and a white five-pointed star above its heads.
era-1914.open: Page said every faction used the same eagle flag and no new flag emerged; the sources read describe several different flags. Occupation garrisons' flag use is not covered.

era-1912.says: Wikipedia: a flag was raised at Vlore on 28 November 1912; no original survives and 'there is no definitive proof' of its appearance; accounts conflict (Eqrem Vlora, Syrja Vlora, Kristo Floqi), and a New York paper printed an illustration on 17 December 1912. FOTW describes no 1912 flag; it dates the Principality flag (eagle with star) to 1914.
era-1912.open: The page states as fact that Qemali raised Skanderbeg's flag; the sources do not settle this.

era-1479.says: Wikipedia: the eagle on red was reused by nationalists in the 19th and early 20th centuries and raised by Ded Gjo Luli at Decic on 6 April 1911; Ottoman merchant flags appear only as an image caption.
era-1479.open: The sources read do not cover vilayet or pashalik flags, local seals, or Ali Pasha's banners; FOTW describes no flags for 1478-1912.

era-1444.says: Wikipedia: Skanderbeg reportedly adopted in 1443 a red flag with a double-headed eagle; it calls the evidence weak (a 15th-century image, a 1598 Henninges illustration, Veronese's 1556 painting). FOTW: on 28 November 1443 Skanderbeg raised a red flag with a black double-headed eagle, his family's standard.
era-1444.open: Page cites Marin Barleti and a goat-horned helmet crest; neither is in the sources read, and Wikipedia describes the evidence as weak rather than 'a real, attested banner'.

era-1962.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1866.open: The page's arms-in-1866 claim is contradicted; sources differ on the date of the 1993 constitution (28 April vs 4 May).

era-1967.says: Wikipedia: the current flag was adopted 27 February 1967, 11 days after royal assent to the West Indies Act 1967, to mark self-government; over 600 people entered the competition, won by Reginald Samuel; full independence 1 November 1981 with the 1967 flag kept. FOTW: flag adopted 27 February 1967 on associated statehood, competition of over 600 entries won by Reginald Samuel, independence 1 November 1981.
era-1967.open: FOTW says a 1994 decision gave the sun seven full points and the page does not confirm that the 1967 flag was identical to today's; FOTW says the flag was apparently adopted for land use at first.

era-1632.says: Wikipedia: the first flag for the territory was created in the late 1950s as a Blue Ensign defaced with the coat of arms (versions 1956-1962 and 1962-1967); the local arms appeared on the Leeward Islands arms in 1909. FOTW: Antigua became a British colony in 1632 and was part of the Leeward Islands 1871-1956, but gives no detail of a colonial Blue Ensign and badge.
era-1632.open: Neither source describes a pineapple-over-sugar-mill badge, or a colonial Blue Ensign before the late 1950s.

era-1861.says: Wikipedia says the flag was officially recognised on 20 July 1816 at Tucumán, that Pueyrredón established the sun flag on 25 January 1818, that on unification in 1861 the national flag replaced Buenos Aires State's flag, that Roca's decree of 25 April 1884 limited the sun flag to government institutions, that decrees of 1943 and Decree 10,302/1944 regulated it, that Law 23,208 of 1985 let individuals use it, and that Decree 1650/2010 standardised colours and proportions. FOTW (Gregoric) says Congress at Tucumán passed the plain triband in 1816, that the Congress, then in Buenos Aires, created the war flag by adding the sun on 25 February 1818, and that the 1884 decree defined the 1:2 ratio and restricted the sun flag to military and government agencies.
era-1861.open: The sources differ on the sun flag's date (25 January or 25 February 1818). FOTW gives only the year for Tucumán, and does not cover 1861. This page used to say the sun flag became the sole civil and state flag.

era-1816.says: Wikipedia says independence was declared on 9 July 1816 and the flag officially recognised on 20 July 1816, and that Pueyrredón established the flag with the Sun of May on 25 January 1818 (a 1944 decree says 25 February). FOTW (Gregoric) says the Tucumán Congress passed the plain triband in 1816 and that the Congress in Buenos Aires added the sun on 25 February 1818.
era-1816.open: The date of the sun differs between sources.

era-1810.says: Wikipedia says Belgrano wrote on 26 February 1812 proposing a national flag, that it was first raised at Rosario on 27 February 1812, that the First Triumvirate ordered him in early March 1812 to stop using it, that he had it blessed at Jujuy on 25 May 1812 and called it the national flag, and that the origin of the colours cannot be accurately established. FOTW (Gregoric) says there are several theories about the design raised on 27 February 1812 and that triband flags were in use by 1814 without the sun.
era-1810.open: This page's «adopted informally as the flag of the patriot army» is close to Wikipedia's account, which also says the government told him to stop.

era-1776.says: Wikipedia says the first flags in the territory were Spanish crown flags and that the last formal Spanish flag was the red and yellow one set by Charles III in 1785; it does not mention the Cross of Burgundy.
era-1776.open: One source; the page text now says its Cross of Burgundy is unconfirmed.

era-1820.says: Wikipedia: Rosas changed the official shade to turquoise blue in 1829; unofficial Rosas-era variants from 1836 had four Phrygian caps and a red Sun of May; Federalist units used dark blue flags and a red-and-white bicolour; after Caseros (1852) the inland provinces returned to light blue with the sun, while the State of Buenos Aires flew a flag of two light blue stripes with a white centre bearing arms until 1861. FOTW's page does not cover the Rosas era or the Confederation.
era-1820.open: The page said no rival flag emerged and everyone flew the same banner; Wikipedia contradicts this. Federal ribbons are not covered.

era-1991.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1920.says: Wikipedia: the Armenian SSR constitution of 2 February 1922 describes a red banner with gold letters; 1936-37 a gold hammer and sickle was added; 1940 the lettering changed; a redesign of 1952 gave a red field with a horizontal blue stripe and a gold hammer and sickle below a star in the canton; the tricolour replaced it on 24 August 1990.
era-1920.open: Flags of the World covers no Soviet-era flag; Wikipedia's description of the stripe position differs from the page's 'near the bottom edge', and the 1920-1952 flags and the 1991 end date are not matched by the single drawing.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia: on 1 August 1918 the National Assembly voted a horizontal tricolour of red, blue and orange (a 19 September 1918 instruction asked for yellow in place of orange cloth); parliament reaffirmed it in June 1919; Soviet troops entered Yerevan 29 November 1920. FOTW: the flag was used 1918-1921 and the red-blue-orange tricolour was readopted on 24 August 1990.
era-1918.open: Neither source read gives the meanings of the colours (blood, sky, courage) stated on the page; the end date differs slightly (Wikipedia late 1920, FOTW 1921).

era-1828.says: Wikipedia: Armenian volunteer militias in the 1826-1828 Russo-Persian War carried flags showing a double-headed eagle, Noah's Ark and Christ; in 1885 Father Ghevont Alishan designed a red, green and white tricolour for a Paris students' association.
era-1828.open: Neither source mentions the black-gold-white imperial tricolour used in Armenian provinces; Flags of the World does not cover this period.

era-1375.says: Wikipedia: after Armenia was divided between the Persian and Ottoman empires 'the idea of an Armenian flag ceased to exist for some time' (no date given); Cilician Armenian flags appear on maps including the Catalan Atlas (1375).
era-1375.open: Wikipedia gives no date for the partition and says nothing of an Ottoman crescent or Safavid roundel as Armenian flags; Flags of the World does not cover the period.

era-1045.says: Wikipedia: Cilician Armenian flags appear on maps (Dalorto 1325, Dulcert 1339, Catalan Atlas 1375); a reconstructed Hasan-Jalalyan standard is shown for 1214-1261.
era-1045.open: Wikipedia does not describe flags under Byzantine, Seljuk or Mongol overlordship; Flags of the World does not cover the period.

era-885.says: Wikipedia: in 885 Armenia gained independence and its flag is described as a dark red canvas with a white leopard and a Christian cross; the 'Ani leopard' survives in the arms of Gyumri. The page does not name the Bagratid dynasty.
era-885.open: Wikipedia's colours (dark red, white leopard) differ from the drawing (blue field, gold cross and disc); Flags of the World does not cover the period.

era-1901.says: Wikipedia says a federal flag competition of April 1901 drew 32,823 entries, the winning design first flew over the Royal Exhibition Building in Melbourne on 3 September 1901 with five near-identical entries sharing the prize, Edward VII's approval was announced on 11 February 1903, the Southern Cross stars were standardised to seven points on 23 February 1903, the Commonwealth Star gained a seventh point on 8 December 1908, and the Flags Act 1953 received royal assent on 14 February 1954. FOTW (Morris) says the competition was announced in the Gazette of 29 April 1901, the flag first flew on 3 September 1901, the King's approval was given in 1902 and confirmed by a proclamation of 20 February 1903, a seventh point was added by the Gazette of 19 December 1908, and the Flags Act 1953 was confirmed in a Gazette of 14 April 1954.
era-1901.open: The sources differ on the 1908 date (8 or 19 December), the 1903 dates, and the 1954 date (14 February assent or 14 April gazette). This page used to say the star was seven-pointed from the start.

era-65.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — pre-colonial era, no single flag».
era-65.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1788.says: Wikipedia says each colony had a flag based on the Blue Ensign with a state badge, that Cook landed at Botany Bay on 29 April 1770 and Phillip raised the Union Jack when proclaiming New South Wales in February 1788, and that the National Colonial Flag was created in 1823–1824.
era-1788.open: One source. FOTW's Australian page does not cover the colonial flags. This page says the Union Jack was the formal ensign of all six colonies; the source describes Blue Ensign badges.

era-1955.says: FOTW says the Flag Act passed by the Austrian parliament on 28 March 1984 put into effect the state flag (red-white-red with the arms) and its 2:3 ratio, and that the plain triband is the national flag and civil ensign. Wikipedia's infobox gives 1 May 1945 for the formal adoption and 28 March 1984 for the state flag, and 1230 for the origin of the design.
era-1955.open: The date a plain red-white-red became Austria's flag again depends on which event is meant: 1945 (restoration), 1955 (this era's start) or 1984 (the Flag Act); the sources read do not give 1955. FOTW also notes the law does not specify the shade of red.

era-1156.says: FOTW quotes Peter Diem: Duke Frederick II (1210–1246), the last Babenberg, adopted the red-white-red arms in 1230, and the first colour document bearing them dates from 1232. Wikipedia says it is first documented in a seal on a deed of 30 November 1230 for Lilienfeld Abbey, and that the Leopold V story (Siege of Acre, 1191) is a legend.
era-1156.open: This is evidence for 1230, not for the whole era from 1156: nothing was found for a red-white-red banner before 1230. Both sources describe arms and colours; whether a banner of this design was flown in the 13th century is not established. Wikipedia's 1230 and 1232 statements carry citation-needed tags.

era-1867.says: Wikipedia says black-yellow was the Habsburg monarchy's national flag, later the Austrian Empire's, until 1918 (citing Preuß, Flaggenlexikon). FOTW says the red-white-red ensign with a shield was adopted as merchant ensign on 20 March 1786, that a dual-monarchy merchant flag was created in 1869 (18 February 1869 decree, in use from 1 August 1869), and that a red-white-red war ensign was used from 1880 until 10 October 1915.
era-1867.open: The image shows an eagle on gold, which is the imperial standard rather than the black-yellow flag the sources describe. This page's statement that red-white-red was «used for the Austrian lands since medieval times» is stronger than the sources: Diem puts the arms in 1230 and FOTW the ensign in 1786.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia says that after Austria-Hungary's dissolution in 1918 German Austria adopted the red-white-red triband, with no law or date given and a citation-needed tag.
era-1918.open: One source. This page's claim that it was the first government in centuries to fly it without an eagle or crown was not checked.

era-1938.says: FOTW (Steven Shea, 1996) says the Austrian flag was not used after the Anschluss of 1938 but was restored with independence in 1945.
era-1938.open: One source, and it does not say what flew instead; this page says the Reich's banner. That is not confirmed here.

era-1945.says: FOTW (Steven Shea, 1996) says the flag was restored with independence in 1945; Wikipedia's infobox gives 1 May 1945 as the formal adoption, with no law or citation named.
era-1945.open: The Allied occupation (1945–1955) is not described by either source; the page's statements about the four zones were not checked.

era-1934.says: Neither Wikipedia nor FOTW describes the 1934-38 flag; FOTW lists 1934-38 only as a heading and Wikipedia does not cover it.
era-1934.open: Fatherland Front, Kruckenkreuz and eagle claims not covered by sources read.

era-1919.says: Wikipedia: German Austria adopted the red-white-red triband in 1918, and the flag was formally adopted 1 May 1945. FOTW lists the First Republic (1919) only as a heading and says the flag was not used after the 1938 Anschluss and was restored in 1945.
era-1919.open: No source read describes the 1919 flag itself or the reason for choosing the colours.

era-1804.says: Wikipedia: the black-yellow flag was the national flag of the Habsburg monarchy and the Austrian Empire; caption dates the Austrian Empire flag c. 1804-1867. FOTW lists the Empire of Austria (1804) only as a heading.
era-1804.open: Eagle-on-gold description and Congress of Vienna claims not covered.

era-1453.says: Wikipedia: Habsburgs took the red-white-red colours after the 1278 Marchfeld battle, linked to the 1283 Treaty of Rheinfelden; Archduchy details are not given.
era-1453.open: FOTW silent; Archduchy banner claim and the 1453 date not covered.

era-1282.says: Wikipedia: first recorded on a deed of 30 Nov 1230 under Frederick II; Ottokar II adopted the colours after 1246; Habsburgs took them after 1278 (Rheinfelden 1283). FOTW: Friedrich II reportedly adopted the arms in 1230, first document dated 1232.
era-1282.open: Sources differ on the first document (Wikipedia 1230, FOTW 1232); neither says the Habsburgs chose the colours over their own.

era-1991.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 9 November 1918; Flags of the World dates it 27 February 1993.
era-1991.open: The two sources do not agree on a year with each other, or one is silent, so 1991, the year this page starts the current flag, could not be confirmed. Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1920.says: Wikipedia: Soviet forces took Baku in April 1920 and banned the 1918 flags; Soviet Azerbaijan's first flag was adopted 19 May 1921 and the eighth and final one on 7 Oct 1952: red with a blue band along the bottom (about a quarter of the height) plus Soviet emblems. Wikipedia's captions date the 1952 flag 1952-1990, its infobox 1952-1991.
era-1920.open: Flags of the World's Azerbaijan page is silent on Soviet-era flags, so only one publisher; the 'light blue' shade and gold hammer and sickle are not stated in the text read.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia: the republic declared independence 28 May 1918 and adopted a first flag (red, white crescent and eight-pointed star) on 21 June 1918; a blue-red-green tricolor with crescent and star on the red band was approved in draft 9 Nov 1918 and raised over parliament 7 Dec 1918; banned after April 1920. FOTW: the flag was used 1918-1920 in a slightly different version from today's, and the star was already on it.
era-1918.open: FOTW does not give the exact 1918 adoption date; the page's colour-meaning gloss is attributed by FOTW to Ali Bey Hussein Zade rather than stated as an official meaning.

era-1813.says: Neither Wikipedia's nor Flags of the World's Azerbaijan flag page describes a flag of the Russian imperial period.
era-1813.open: The page's description of this era's flag is not covered by the sources read. No source read confirms the black-gold-white tricolor as used over the Azerbaijani provinces.

era-1747.says: Neither Wikipedia's nor Flags of the World's Azerbaijan flag page describes a flag of the Persian-suzerain khanates.

era-1830.says: Wikipedia says insurgents replaced the French flag on Brussels city hall on 27 August 1830 with a horizontal red-yellow-black tricolour, and that on 23 January 1831 the National Congress enshrined the tricolour without setting the stripe order, the stripes changing from horizontal to vertical that day, with the modern form (black at the hoist) reached on 12 October 1831. FOTW says the first true national flag in 1830 was horizontal red-yellow-black, that the Provisional Government decreed on 23 January 1831 that the colours be placed vertically, that the Navy set black at the hoist on 15 September 1831 and the Interior Department on 12 October 1831, that horizontal and vertical flags coexisted until 24 September 1838, and that the colours come from the arms of Brabant.
era-1830.open: The sources differ on who acted on 23 January 1831 (the National Congress or the Provisional Government). This page used to say vertical black-yellow-red was adopted within days of the uprising and as a homage to revolutionary France; neither source says either. The drawing shows the later vertical form.

era-1889.says: Wikipedia says a provisional flag inspired by the US flag flew from 15 to 19 November 1889 until Deodoro da Fonseca vetoed it, that Decree No. 4 of 19 November 1889 legally replaced the monarchy's flag, that Raimundo Teixeira Mendes, Miguel Lemos, Manuel Pereira Reis and Décio Villares designed the new one, that the 1889 flag had 21 stars, that stars were added on 21 April 1960 (Guanabara), 30 May 1968 (Acre) and under Law No. 8,421 of 11 May 1992, and that Law No. 5,700 of 1 September 1971 sets the construction. FOTW says Decree No. 4 of 19 November 1889 established the basic design, that Benjamin Constant prepared the decree, that the sphere depicts Rio's sky on 15 November 1889, that the original had 21 stars, and that Law 5443 of 28 May 1968 modified the flag.
era-1889.open: The sources disagree about Law 8421: FOTW dates it 1972 in one place and 1992 in another, and Wikipedia's body says it added four stars in one section and six in another. FOTW does not cover the 1960 change.

era-1822.says: Wikipedia says Pedro I's decree of 18 September 1822 marks the independent Kingdom's flag, that Debret designed the royal standard that became the imperial flag (citation needed), that green stood for the House of Braganza and yellow for the House of Habsburg, that the first imperial flag is captioned as having 19 stars, and that Law No. 704 of 29 August 1853 added a 20th star for Paraná. FOTW says Brazilian flag historians attribute the lozenge design to Debret, that Pedro signed three decrees on 18 September 1822 including one creating the green-and-yellow cockade, and that the imperial flag carried an armillary sphere as its central charge.
era-1822.open: The star count changed within this era (19 stars, then 20 in 1853, and more later), so the single drawing cannot be right for all of 1822–1889.

era-1815.says: Wikipedia says Brazil was raised to a kingdom united with Portugal and the Algarves in 1815 (citation needed), that a charter of 1816 gave Brazil arms of a gold armillary sphere on a blue field, and that the flag was the United Kingdom's flag, whose design the article does not describe. FOTW (Palac) says the Red Ensign, created in 1707 as the Merchant Navy ensign, was used on sea and land from 1870 and authorised at sea as the Red Canadian Ensign in 1892.
era-1867.open: FOTW describes a parliamentary resolution of 18 December 1964 approving continued use of the Union flag as a Commonwealth symbol. This page's «only fully official flag» is stronger than Wikipedia's «de facto».

era-1848.says: FOTW (credited to Željko Heimer) says the red-white-blue tricolour was first used as a flag in 1848, a drawing of a Slavic barricade in Vienna being the first documented use, and that a tricolour in the Varaždin Town Museum dates from 1848 or a few years later. Wikipedia's «Flag of Croatia» has the tricolour in use in 1848, without a citation.
era-1848.open: The pan-Slavic colours «formally adopted that same year at the Prague Slavic Congress», stated on this page, were not checked. FOTW says the tricolour was banned from 1852 (imperial decree of 10 September 1852) and reintroduced about 1860; the page's single year does not show that.

era-1868.says: FOTW says the state flag with the arms was in use from 1867 and adopted in 1868 under the Nagodba, with the Crown of St Stephen; an edict of 16 September 1876 specified the crown; a viceroy's decree of 21 November 1914 (no. 8378) named the red-white-blue tricolour the civil flag of Croatia and Slavonia; and the official arms stayed in use until 29 October 1918. Wikipedia says the civil flag was in use, citing Boršak-Marijanović (1996) for the arms variant.
era-1868.open: FOTW notes that Dalmatia was in the Austrian half and that unofficial variants existed (other crowns, none, other shields). The page's remark that the flag asserted «a unity the empire never actually granted» is interpretation and was not sourced.

era-1809.says: Wikipedia dates the Illyrian Provinces to 1809–1814/1815 (Treaty of Schönbrunn, 14 October 1809; formal Austrian annexation 9 June 1815; citing Malkovic, 2011) and shows the French flag in its infobox, but describes no distinct provincial flag.
era-1809.open: That the French tricolour was flown over the provinces rests on the infobox image alone. This page ends the era in 1813; Wikipedia has Austria recovering the area in 1813–1814.

era-1527.says: Wikipedia says the checkerboard is first attested as a decorative symbol of the Kingdom of Croatia in 1495 (an Innsbruck tower showing Maximilian I's emblem; Hesmer 2008, Neubecker, Hye 1993) and appears officially on a seal of the Cetingrad Charter of 1527; that historically the first field was mostly white, with no official standard until the 19th century; and that modern scholars think Habsburg influence probable.
era-1527.open: Whether the checkerboard was flown as a flag in this period, rather than carried as arms, is not established by the source read. The swatch shows the first square red, as on today's flag. This page used to say the symbol «becomes fixed after 1527»; the source says it had no fixed form until the 19th century.

era-1918.says: FOTW (credited to Željko Heimer) describes the flag as blue-white-red, used before the law and formally introduced with the 1921 constitution, and prescribed as the civil and state ensign by Article 2 of the 1922 law. Wikipedia gives the 1922 law as the first official adoption (Službene Novine Kraljevine SHS no. 89, 28 February 1922) and a 1918 start in its infobox.
era-1918.open: Wikipedia's infobox (1918) and its text (1922) disagree on adoption. This page used to say the regional tricolours «kept their own orderings»; neither source says that, and FOTW reports the 1929 dictatorship reportedly banned them, unclear whether enforced.

era-1929.says: FOTW says there was apparently no change in the flag law when the kingdom was proclaimed in 1929, and that the 1937 law did not change it. Wikipedia dates the renaming to 3 October 1929 and shows the same blue-white-red flag.
era-1929.open: FOTW adds that the 1929 dictatorship reportedly banned national tricolours such as the Croatian one in favour of the Yugoslav one, and that it is unclear whether this was enforced (Heimer, 2009). This page used to say Croatian politicians resisted through the 1930s; no source for that was found.

era-1939.says: FOTW says all sources seem to agree that the Croatian tricolour was used after 1939, that its use was governed by natural law and not by any written regulation, that a version with the coat of arms in the centre was reportedly for state use, and that the crownless arms seem not to have been official though crownless versions were used on flags. Wikipedia's «Flag of Croatia» has a similar flag without the crown above the checkerboard, uncited.
era-1939.open: No decree for the flag was found, which agrees with the page's «by custom». Wikipedia's Banovina article describes no flag and dates the Cvetković–Maček Agreement to 24 August 1939 and the Banovina's de jure existence to 1945.

era-1941.says: FOTW quotes the law-decree signed by Ante Pavelić on 28 April 1941 and published in Narodne novine no. 15 on 30 April: three horizontal fields red, white, blue, with the state arms (25 fields, the first white) in the middle of the white field and, on the red field near the hoist, a curl enclosing a white field with a dark blue letter U. Wikipedia describes the crown removed, a U added at the top left and the first field white, without a citation.
era-1941.open: The older red-white-blue civil flag stayed in use everywhere except on state or local administration buildings until further regulation (FOTW). The decree text was read only as quoted by FOTW.

era-1943.says: FOTW says the state was Democratic Federal Yugoslavia from 29 November 1943, that before 1946 the red star usually sat in the white field without a yellow edge, and dates the red-star flag to 1941 (July, Heimer; September, Smith 1975). Wikipedia describes the red star added to the white band and the ratio changed from 2:3 to 1:2, with a citation-needed tag.
era-1943.open: Wikipedia's account of this period has no citation. The page's phrase that communism was «laid directly over the old kingdom's flag» is interpretation and was not sourced.

era-1946.says: Both give 31 January 1946 and the new constitution for the yellow-edged red-star flag. FOTW credits Đorđe Andrejević-Kun with the design (Wikipedia has a citation-needed tag on this) and says the state was renamed the Socialist Federal Republic on 7 April 1963 with the flag unchanged.
era-1946.open: The end differs: FOTW says the flag was abandoned in spring 1991 and the federation's name ended on 15 January 1992; Wikipedia's infobox gives 27 April 1992 with a citation-needed tag. This page ends the era in 1992.

era-1947.says: FOTW says the red-white-blue flag with a yellow-bordered red star was officially adopted on 18 January 1947 and officially abandoned on 25 June 1990, and quotes Article 7 of the 1974 constitution for a red five-pointed star in the centre. Wikipedia has the star with a yellow border replacing the arms in 1947, and the arms returning in May 1990.
era-1947.open: The end is June 1990 in FOTW and May 1990 in Wikipedia; this page says 1990. Wikipedia names no adopter for the 1947 flag.

era-1991.says: FOTW (Heimer, 2013) quotes Article 6 of the 1992 constitution, proclaimed 19 December 1991 and published 2 January 1992, prescribing the Serb tricolour with the colours from top to bottom red, blue, white, and says the flag was never formally changed. Wikipedia's article on the republic gives the same constitution date and shows a flag image but describes no flag; the separate flag article also gives no colours or date.
era-1991.open: One source for the flag itself, so it is not attested.

era-1420.says: Wikipedia says the Lion of St Mark was shown with an open book in peacetime and with an upright sword in war, citing Flags of the World's Venice page, and dates the flag's relinquishment to 1797.
era-1420.open: That this was the flag flown in Dalmatia from 1420 is not stated by the source read. The Flags of the World Venice page was not read.

era-1358.says: FOTW, quoting Josip Luetić (1967), says the 1272 Statutes made the flag official as «VIXILLUM S. BLASIJ» and that it flew on Dubrovnik ships until 27 December 1807, when General Lauriston ordered it replaced; a white flag inscribed Libertas is described as a secondary ensign. Wikipedia describes St Blaise's flag as white with gold edging, the patron saint of the Republic, and a surviving flag over 200 years old, citing Britannica.
era-1358.open: The end differs by a year: FOTW gives 27 December 1807 for the flag, this page and the era's title say 1808. FOTW says a Libertas flag on a Croatian stamp was never used in Dubrovnik. The page's statement that Libertas was among the earliest civic mottoes flown as a flag in Europe was not sourced.

era-925.says: Neither source describes a flag, banner or device for the Kingdom of Croatia 925-1102; Flags of the World cites Heimer (1995) that red and white refer to early medieval Croatian states, undated.
era-925.open: No source read dates the earliest checkerboard or any medieval Croatian banner, or mentions a star-over-crescent device.

era-1902.open: Wikipedia's own references differ on the 1906 date.

era-1918.says: FOTW (Sache) says the white-red flag was first officially hoisted in Washington on 18 October 1918, at Masaryk's residence, and was identical to Poland's. Wikipedia says the National Assembly approved the flag with a blue hoist triangle on 30 March 1920 to distinguish it from Poland's, after Jaroslav Kursa's 1919 proposal.
era-1918.open: Explanations of the blue differ (the third Slavic colour in use since 1848; a nod to Slovaks; Slovak mountains called «late mythology»). Wikipedia marks the rationale citation-needed. This page used to say the blue represented Slovakia and Ruthenia.

era-1945.says: Wikipedia says the 1920–1939 flag was restored in 1945 (citation needed) and gives 1945–1992 as the flag's use.
era-1945.open: One source; FOTW's Czech page does not cover 1945. Neither source describes 1945–1948 in detail.

era-1198.says: Wikipedia says that from 1253 a two-tailed silver lion on red was the arms of the Kingdom of Bohemia (citing Czech sources), that a legend in Dalimil's chronicle ties the second tail to Přemysl Otakar I's help against the Saxons, and that the kings used a black eagle on silver in the first half of the 13th century.
era-1198.open: This page used to credit Přemysl Otakar II. Whether the lion banner was flown as a flag is not stated.

era-1158.says: Wikipedia says the lion was first shown with one tail and that Emperor Frederick granted Vladislaus II a silver lion on red (no year, citation needed).
era-1158.open: The page's statement that it is attested on ducal seals from this period was not found in the source.

era-1948.says: Wikipedia: the 1920 flag (approved 30 March 1920) was restored in 1945 and, as listed for 1945-1992, was one of only three socialist-country flags in Europe without the coat of arms at the centre; captions give separate naval ensigns and a war flag (1960-1990). FOTW records no emblem or flag change in the communist period and says the Czechoslovak flag remained in use; a 1968 idea of separate Czech symbols was dropped after the Warsaw Pact invasion.
era-1948.open: Neither source mentions a 1948 event, the comparison with Hungary or Poland, or a presidential flag in the communist period; Wikipedia gives no dates for this period.

era-1938.says: Wikipedia labels the 1920-1939 flag as used by the First and Second Czechoslovak Republics, but covers the Second Republic only through that label. FOTW does not cover 1938-1939.
era-1938.open: The territorial losses and the 'fading claim' framing are not covered.

era-1526.says: Wikipedia: the traditional colours derive from an 1192 coat of arms, a rampant lion with double silver tail on red, and the Kingdom of Bohemia's flag is shown 'until 1918'. FOTW: the Bohemian arms were a white lion on red. Neither covers the Habsburg period.
era-1526.open: The lion banner flown unchanged under Habsburg rule, 1526-1918, is not described by either source.

era-1814.says: Wikipedia says a regulation of 1748 (11 June in its infobox, 11 July in the Danish title it cites) set the merchant-ship flag and its proportions, that private use was outlawed by a circular of 7 January 1834 and the ban repealed by a regulation of 7 July 1854 (the swallow-tailed Splitflag excluded), and that the Guinness record for the oldest continuously used national flag dates from 1625. FOTW says regulations of 11 July 1748 set the proportions (28:34 per Southworth) and that regulations of 1 May 1893 allowed up to 28:37.
era-1814.open: The 1748 date differs by a month between Wikipedia's own sources. The German occupation of 1940–45 is not covered by either source.

era-1219.open: Neither source supports a flag of 1219 itself. This page used to say the design was unchanged for eight centuries.

era-1243.says: Neither source covers Mongol-era flags; Flags of the World says only that Giorgi V drove out the Mongols, with no date or flag detail.

era-1008.says: Wikipedia: five-cross banner dated to the 12th century; supposed single red cross on white for Vakhtang I; Tamar tradition of a dark red cross and star on white; a coin of David IV found in 2021 shows a folded five-cross composition. era-1008.open: The page's maroon field with gold cross is not confirmed by either source; no dated Bagrationi seal, coin or donor-portrait evidence of such a flag was found in the pages read.

era-1990.open: The flag itself is the one adopted in 1949 (Basic Law, Article 22); 1990 is when it became the flag of the reunified country.

era-1949.says: Wikipedia says Article 22 of the Basic Law of 23 May 1949 reads «The federal flag shall be black, red and gold», and that East Germany also used black-red-gold in 1949–59. FOTW (Sensen) says the GDR's tricolour had no coat of arms in 1949–1959 and carried one in 1959–1989.
era-1949.open: The sources differ on the West German date: FOTW gives 8 or 9 May 1949 (about two weeks before the Federal Republic existed), Wikipedia 23 May 1949. The 1 October 1959 GDR emblem law was not found in the part of Wikipedia that was read.

era-1933.says: Wikipedia says a ruling of 12 March 1933 made two flags legal, black-white-red and the Nazi Party flag, and banned black-red-gold, and that on 15 September 1935 the dual arrangement ended with the Nazi flag the sole national flag. FOTW says the Third Reich replaced the tricolour with its own flag on 12 March 1933.
era-1933.open: The image is a stylised abstraction, not a reproduction.

era-1918.says: FOTW (Sensen) says the tricolour was re-adopted as the Weimar Republic's flag on 11 August 1919. Wikipedia says the Weimar constitution designated black-red-gold in 1919, that black-white-red was kept as a civil ensign with the new flag in the canton and as a merchant flag in 1919–1933, and that black-white-red was reintroduced for diplomatic missions abroad in 1922.
era-1918.open: This page used to say black-red-gold became a national flag «for the first time»; Wikipedia says the Frankfurt Parliament declared it official in 1848–49. «11 August» is FOTW's; Wikipedia gives only «August 1919».

era-1871.says: Wikipedia says the North German Confederation's 1867 constitution declared black-white-red the civil and war ensign and that the 1871 constitution kept it. FOTW says the Empire chose a flag based on north German traditions, Bismarck favouring a Kleindeutschland solution, and gives no separate date for the 1871 decision.
era-1871.open: This page's explanation of the colours (Prussian black-white plus Hanseatic red-white) was not found in either source.

era-1866.says: Wikipedia says the North German Confederation's constitution of 1867 declared black-white-red a civil and war ensign (1866–67 covers its creation).
era-1866.open: The page's claim that it was «the very first appearance of black-white-red», and its explanation of the colours, were not confirmed; FOTW's Germany page does not cover the North German Confederation.

era-1815.says: Wikipedia says the Bundestag adopted the black-red-gold tricolour on 9 March 1848, that the Frankfurt Parliament declared it the official colours in 1848–49, and that the German Confederation was restored in 1850; its origins are in Jena's Urburschenschaft (1815) and the Lützow Free Corps. FOTW says the Frankfurt Parliament adopted it in 1848 for a proposed united German Empire and that it was abolished in 1852.
era-1815.open: Wikipedia contradicts itself on whether the Confederation had a flag of its own. This page used to say the tricolour «was never the Confederation's official flag»; that is not what the sources say for 1848–52. Prussia's black eagle on white, shown beside it, was not covered by either source.

era-962.says: Wikipedia says black and gold were the emperor's colours and the imperial banner showed a black eagle on gold, its claws and beak red after the late 13th or early 14th century.
era-962.open: One source. It does not say the eagle was double-headed throughout, as this page does.

era-1966.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 6 March 1957.
era-1966.open: The two sources do not agree on a year with each other, or one is silent, so 1966, the year this page starts the current flag, could not be confirmed. Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1295.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — earliest Akan states, no flag or war banner survives».
era-1295.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1964.says: Wikipedia: January 1964 variant with white replacing yellow (CPP colours), resembling Hungary's flag. FOTW: white middle stripe 1 Jan 1964-28 Feb 1966.
era-1964.open: Both sources agree on a white stripe and the period; the page's caption and drawing show an eagle that neither supports, so the drawing needs checking and the star is undescribed.

era-1957.says: Both: red-gold-green with a black star adopted at independence March 1957, designed by Theodosia Okoh; colour meanings red blood, gold minerals, green forest; star tied to Black Star Line (Wikipedia 6 March 1957; FOTW 'lone star of African freedom').
era-1957.open: Wikipedia says this flag ran to 1962 (Union of African States flags in between), the page says 1964; unresolved.

era-1821.says: Wikipedia: Gold Coast flag 1877-1957 was a defaced Blue Ensign replaced by the national flag; design not described.
era-1821.open: FOTW only links; the 1821 start, Union Flag role and Red Ensign are uncovered.

era-1974.says: Wikipedia says Law 48/1975 and Presidential Decree 515/1975 took effect on 7 June 1975 making the former land flag the sole flag, that in 1978 the sea flag returned as the sole flag, that its adoption date is 22 December 1978, and that Law 851/1978 describes it as cyan and white with five cyan and four white stripes (the exact blue left to flagmakers). FOTW (Adams) says the plain cross flag was the only national flag from June 1975 until December 1978, that the striped flag was adopted by law on 22 December 1978, and gives Pantone 286 C as a reference blue.
era-1974.open: The shade of blue is unspecified in law; Pilalis says the lighter blue belongs to the defunct kingdom's arms and the flags use dark blue. This page used to say the nine-stripe flag was unchanged since the 19th century.

era-1204.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1967.says: Wikipedia says a decree of 18 August 1969 made the sea flag the sole national flag, the ratio changed from 2:3 to 7:12 on 18 August 1970, dark blue became increasingly common from the late 1960s (citation needed), and the monarchy was abolished on 1 June 1973.
era-1967.open: One source. This page's «phoenix emblem on seals» was not checked.

era-1924.says: Wikipedia says the Second Hellenic Republic removed the crowns from all flags on 25 March 1924, after crowns had replaced the arms in a decree of 28 December 1863, and that the 2:3 ratio was set on 20 February 1930.
era-1924.open: One source. This page used to say the flag had no crown to remove.

era-1832.says: Wikipedia says the first official naval ensign specifications under Otto were published in 1833 with the royal arms on the cross, that crowns replaced the arms by a decree of 28 December 1863, and that a decree of 26 September 1867 set the shape and use of flags. FOTW says the striped flag was approved in 1832.
era-1832.open: The two sources differ by a year, and neither says the plain striped flag was the kingdom's state flag throughout, as this page used to say.

era-1821.says: Wikipedia says the First National Assembly at Epidaurus officially adopted the flag on 13 January 1822 and that Provisional Government Decree 540 of 15 March 1822 set the land flag, naval ensign and civil ensign. FOTW (Adams) says the striped flag and the plain white cross on blue both date from 1822, the nine stripes said to stand for the nine syllables of the motto «Freedom or Death».
era-1821.open: The meaning of the colours (blue for sea and sky, white for purity), stated on this page, was not found in either source. The syllable explanation is the one given.

era-1941.says: Wikipedia says the Axis occupation of 1941–1944 forbade the Greek flag, which became a symbol of resistance.
era-1941.open: One source. The government-in-exile's flag is not described.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia gives only caption dates (the 1863 flag pattern used 1935-1941 and 1944-1969) and notes a 1967 Compulsory Law 198 on regional flag days that did not change the flag. FOTW does not cover this period.
era-1944.open: Restoration of the monarchy, the civil war and 'unbroken legal continuity' are not covered by either source.

era-1935.says: Wikipedia says Kondylis declared the monarchy restored on 10 October 1935 and a decree of 7 November 1935 reinstated the 31 May 1914 decree (crown flags); a caption dates the 1863 pattern to 1935-1941. It does not name Metaxas. FOTW does not cover the period.
era-1935.open: Metaxas-era symbolism in propaganda and the claim that the flag was never altered are not covered.

era-1913.says: Wikipedia gives only a decree of 31 May 1914 making the crown flag the state flag for ministries and civil services; it gives no other detail for 1913-1924. FOTW does not cover the period.
era-1913.open: Balkan Wars, the wartime split and 1922 catastrophe are not covered as flag history.

era-1261.open: The black double-headed eagle design and its use for the Despotate of the Morea are not covered.

era-1949.says: FOTW (Molnár, 2001) says the flag bore the Rákosi coat of arms in 1949–1956 and that the tricolour was in use again from 1956. Wikipedia says the Rákosi arms became the badge in 1949, that revolutionaries cut the emblem out in 1956, and that on 23 May 1957 the pure tricolour became the official state flag, the new arms never officially placed on it (Act II of 1957).
era-1949.open: The image shows the 1949–1956 flag, so it is evidence for those years only; for 1957–1989 both sources say the plain tricolour was official. This page used to describe the arms as a «1957 redesign»; that was wrong.

era-1946.says: Wikipedia: in 1946-1949 the badge arms lost the crown and a flag with the Kossuth arms was used, again in 1956-1957; communist arms with a red star were added in 1949. FOTW: the tricolour used 1919-1949 and the Rakosi arms 1949-1956; it does not address 1946-1949 specifically.
era-1946.open: The page's plain tricolour without any emblem is not supported; whether the Kossuth arms appeared on the flag is stated only by Wikipedia.

era-1920.says: FOTW says the tricolour was in use again in 1919–1949 and, quoting the DK book (Phil Nelson, 1999), that until 1945 the royal crown appeared in the centre of the national flag. Wikipedia says the tricolour appears with minor arms in 1920–1944/45, hedging («it seems») and noting a version without arms was also used.
era-1920.open: Both sources are hedged or second-hand on whether the arms were on the flag; the page's description of the shield is not confirmed.

era-1919.says: FOTW (Molnár, 2001) gives 21 March–31 July 1919 for the Hungarian Soviet Republic's red flag. Wikipedia says it used a solid red banner for about four and a half months.
era-1919.open: Neither source says the republic rejected the tricolour as a bourgeois relic, as this page does.

era-1918.says: FOTW says the tricolour was in use in 1867–1919. Wikipedia captions the Károlyi-era flag of the short-lived Hungarian People's Republic in 1918–1919.
era-1918.open: The page's claim that this was the first time the tricolour was stripped of royal emblems «in Hungary's history» was not checked; Wikipedia says the tricolour was used without arms at other times.

era-1867.says: FOTW says the tricolour was in use in 1867–1919 and that after 1848 it represented the Hungarian state within the Empire (Heimer, 2000). Wikipedia says that after the Compromise of 1867 the tricolour became official again, with the Kossuth minor arms as a badge, until 1918.
era-1867.open: The caption describes a crest; the sources describe the tricolour with a badge.

era-1699.says: Wikipedia says red-white-green colours were visible at Leopold II's coronation in 1790, were formally described in 1806, and were mandated by Act XXI of 1848. FOTW records the official colours of the Kingdom as red, white and green in 1806 and Law XXI of 1848 restoring the national colour and arms; it says Hungary was under Austrian occupation from 1849 to 1867.
era-1699.open: This supports the tricolour from 1790 or 1806 to 1867, not for 1699–1790. Both sources give earlier dates that conflict (1608, with Wikipedia saying there is no evidence).

era-1000.says: Wikipedia: the Árpád stripes are the flag of the royal House of Árpád and became increasingly common in the later medieval period; silk cords in red, white and green appear on document seals from the 15th century. era-1000.open: The page's 13th-century seal attestation is not supported; the date the stripes were first attested is not stated by either source.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia: the tricolour carried the minor arms 1920 to 1944-1945, and a version without arms was also used; the Arrow Cross era flag or emblem is not covered. FOTW does not mention the Arrow Cross.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia: a commission submitted a protocol for the yellow-green-red tricolour on 19 April 1918 and the Council accepted it; the 1922 constitution adopted the tricolour. FOTW: 19 April 1918 approval by the commission; December 1905 the red flag with a white knight was proposed by Basanavičius and rejected because red suggested revolution.
era-1918.open: Neither source says the tricolour was chosen because it lacked a heraldic precedent; that motive was dropped.

era-1569.says: Wikipedia: the Vytis red banner with a mounted knight was used at the 1410 Battle of Grunwald and was the Grand Duchy's flag until the late 18th century. FOTW: Guagnini in 1578 describes a red silk flag with a white mounted knight under the ducal crown.
era-1569.open: Wikipedia does not say the rider was white; the Polish Eagle contrast is not in either source.

era-1253.says: FOTW: a 1337 chronicle mentions a Lithuanian flag burned at Bajerburg without describing it; Długosz has Vytautas bring 40 regiments with red banners, 30 bearing a mounted knight, to Tannenberg; Guagnini (1578) gives a white knight on red. Wikipedia: Vytis used at Grunwald in 1410.
era-1253.open: The page's earlier claim of attestation from the 14th century is not in the sources; the first description of the knight is 1410.

era-1795.says: WP: the Vytis was the Grand Duchy's flag until annexation by Russia; no detail 1795-1904; 1905 Great Seimas favoured the tricolour over the Vytis. FOTW: Lithuania Minor flag (green-white-red) known from the 17th century, Lithuanian-American association flags in the later 19th century, 1905 proposal of the white knight on red.
era-1795.open: Russian imperial tricolour over Lithuania and the claim that no Lithuanian flag existed are not covered; neither source describes bans.

era-1965.says: Wikipedia: independence from the UK in 1965 removed the black-and-white striped hoist, giving the modern design (green rectangle on red with a white crescent), adopted 25 July 1965; Sultan's Standard 1965-1968, Presidential Standard from 1968. FOTW: current flag adopted 25 July 1965, hoist strip withdrawn in 1965, the Sultanate ended about three years after independence.
era-1965.open: FOTW cites Crampton for the current national and presidential flags being introduced officially on 26 July 1968, which conflicts with 1965; the sources read do not reconcile the dates.

era-1954.says: Wikipedia: the Sultanate was restored in 1954 but the flag was not changed back; a Sultan's flag with a five-pointed star was made for 1954-1965. FOTW: the Sultan was reinstated in 1954 with no changes to the flags. Neither source describes a white-bordered black panel at this date.
era-1954.open: The drawing (red field, black panel, crescent) is not confirmed by either source; Wikipedia's national flag after 1953 is the crescent-reversed design, not a black panel.

era-1953.says: Wikipedia: when the Maldives became a republic in 1953 the national flag was dropped and the state flag's crescent was reversed to face the hoist. FOTW: in 1953-54 the crescent was turned to face the fly and the Government service flag became the national flag. Both place the crescent before 1953 (Wikipedia: added between 1926 and 1932; FOTW: early 20th century, horns toward hoist until 1949).
era-1953.open: Neither source says the crescent was newly added in 1953, or mentions Arabic calligraphy; the drawing is unconfirmed.

era-1887.says: Wikipedia: a plain red flag with a black-and-white striped hoist (the Dhandimathi, undated) was in use to early in the 20th century; its image labels conflict (1796-1903 vs 1903-1926); the crescent was added between 1926 and 1932 by Abdul Majeed Didi. FOTW: red banner with black and white stripes added at the hoist (a 1965 source says oblique); Prime Minister Abdul Majid Didi introduced the green panel and crescent in the early 20th century.
era-1887.open: Neither source mentions a black panel inscribed with the Shahada, a c.1903 date for it, or Sultan Muhammad Shamsuddin III; the sources read do not date the striped hoist.

era-1573.says: Wikipedia: the first flag was a plain red field (caption dates 1117-1796); a black-and-white striped hoist was added later (undated). FOTW: the flag was originally a plain red banner, later given black and white stripes at the hoist; undated.
era-1573.open: Neither source mentions the Portuguese interlude or a restoration after 1573; the page's statement that the red field stayed unmodified until the twentieth century is not what the sources say (the striped hoist is undated).

era-1558.says: Neither Wikipedia nor FOTW mentions the Portuguese occupation of Male or any flag for it; Wikipedia's captions date the plain red flag 1117-1796, which overlaps this span.

era-1139.says: Wikipedia says the Battle of Ourique legend of 1139 is pure myth, that the quinas as five escutcheons date from Sancho I in 1185 (verification needed), that the red bordure with castles has a weakly founded link to the 1249 Algarve conquest, that John I added the green Aviz cross in 1385, and that seven castles were fixed in 1578. FOTW says the blue of the escutcheons is always medium or dark blue, never sky blue, a tradition not written down anywhere.
era-1139.open: Wikipedia marks much of this verification-needed. Whether a banner of this design was flown in the 12th century is not stated.

era-1926.says: Wikipedia: the republic's flag was announced in 1910 and its decree published 19 June 1911 (regulations 30 June 1911); FOTW: flag and arms adopted 30 June 1911 and the constitution refers to the flag of the 5 October 1910 revolution. Neither says anything about 1926-1974.
era-1926.open: Whether the Estado Novo kept the flag unchanged, and the comparisons with Spain, are not covered by the sources read; this is not a finding that it changed.

era-1971.says: Both sources date the current flag to 1949, before this era begins in 1971, so the flag was already in use at the start. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 9 July 1971; Flags of the World dates it 09 Jul 1971.
era-1971.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1916.says: Wikipedia: 1916 treaty with Britain (the nine points stand for the ninth reconciled emirate); in 1932 the British Navy suggested an official flag and Qatar added the nine-pointed serrated edge, diamonds and the word 'Qatar'; maroon was standardised in 1936; the wording and diamonds were removed in the 1960s; adopted 9 July 1971. FOTW: the distinctive flag emerged in the 1930s and in about 1949 the plain flag came into use with the colour altered from red to maroon.
era-1916.open: The sources disagree on the date maroon was fixed (Wikipedia 1936, FOTW c.1949); neither uses the word 'protectorate' and neither describes the page's intermediate plain white hoist band.

era-1868.says: Wikipedia: Qatar's historic flag, 18th century to 1860, was plain red, linked to the Kharijite leader Qatari ibn al-Fuja'a (the link is undated).
era-1868.open: Neither Wikipedia nor FOTW mentions the 1868 events or Bahrain's separate treaty position; the red flag 'shared across the coast' is not covered.

era-1783.says: Wikipedia: Qatar's historic flag from the 18th century to 1860 was plain red, linked to Qatari ibn al-Fuja'a, which describes a Qatari red flag rather than a Bahraini one.

era-1871.says: Neither Wikipedia's nor FOTW's Qatar page covers the Ottoman period; Wikipedia says only that a white vertical hoist stripe was added in the 19th century 'to suit the British directive' (no year).
era-1871.open: The Ottoman garrison banners and Al Thani local flag in this era are not described by any source read.

era-1989.says: Wikipedia says protesters in Timișoara on 20 December 1989 waved flags with the Communist arms cut out, and that on 27 December 1989 the National Salvation Front restored the simple tricolour of 1867. era-1989.open: The instrument of 27 December 1989 is not named by either source.

era-1947.says: FOTW (Neumann) says that after the communist takeover in 1948 the tricolour was charged with a new coat of arms of Soviet inspiration. Wikipedia says Romania became a people's republic on 30 December 1947 and royal symbols were outlawed (citation needed), that a 1948 emblem showed a rising sun, tractor, oil drill and wheat, that a red star was added in 1952 and that the arms changed in 1965 (all citation needed).
era-1947.open: FOTW does not cover 1965. This page used to say the coat of arms formally replaced the royal one in 1965; neither source says so.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia's coat-of-arms article says that after Transylvania joined Romania its arms went in the fourth quarter and Banat's in the third, and that the lesser arms appeared in the Official Gazette no. 92 of 29 July 1921. FOTW says the tricolour was codified in 1872 as a plain tricolour with the arms on military and naval ensigns.
era-1918.open: This page used to date the new arms to 1922; the source gives 1921. Whether the flag was unchanged at the union is not described by either source.

era-1859.says: Wikipedia says the United Principalities used a red-yellow-blue horizontal tricolour in 1859–1866 and that the vertical order, blue at the hoist, yellow, red at the fly, was set on 26 March 1867. FOTW says the tricolour became the national flag in 1859 under Cuza, horizontal with blue on top until 1862 and red on top from 1862 to 1867, and that sources differ on the switch to vertical (Heimer 1866, Neumann 1867).
era-1859.open: The sources disagree on which colour was on top in 1859–62, so the drawing follows Wikipedia. This page used to say a vertical tricolour was adopted in 1861–62, and that it fused Wallachia's blue and yellow with Moldavia's red; neither source says that.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia: on 30 December 1947 Romania was proclaimed a people's republic and the royal coat of arms and tricolors showing it were outlawed; the 1867 tricolor is its Kingdom-era flag (1881-1947).
era-1944.open: Neither source read covers the 1944-47 flag specifically.

era-1940.says: Wikipedia gives the 1867 tricolor for the Kingdom 1881-1947; Flags of the World jumps from the 1867/1872 arrangements to 1948.
era-1940.open: Neither source mentions Antonescu, the Iron Guard, or any change in 1940-44.

era-1881.says: Wikipedia: vertical blue-yellow-red set 26 March 1867; arms only on army and princely flags; 1872 law changed the arms. Flags of the World: 1872 codification as plain tricolor, ensigns with arms; kingdom proclaimed under Charles but no flag change given.
era-1881.open: Neither source describes an 1881 flag change, a royal crown on a state flag, or Hohenzollern arms.

era-1600.says: Wikipedia: Michael the Brave's flag, black eagle on a green juniper branch with a cross in its beak, damask yellow-white faded to white (undated). Flags of the World: c. 1593-1601 white banner with raven, juniper and double cross; 1532-35 red banner with bird on peak; 1688-1714 Brancoveanu personal flag; 1834 Ghika tricolor with eagle on the yellow band.
era-1600.open: A black eagle on a gold field as a 17th-18th century princely flag is not stated by either source.

era-1600-1.says: Flags of the World: 1457-1504 Stephen III red great banner with aurochs head, star, sun and moon; c. 1600 Jeremiah Movila red banner with aurochs head and two crescent moons; 1834 Sturdza blue militia standards; 1842-48 Bibesco red flag. Wikipedia: Moldavian arms and flags in blue, yellow, red, no dates.
era-1600-1.open: Black aurochs head and the rose are not stated; Wikipedia gives no dated Moldavian design.

era-82bce.says: Flags of the World cites a claim that Dacian standard colours appear on Trajan's Column, describing a metal wolf's head with coloured cloth bands, and says such statements are disputable.
era-82bce.open: No source read dates the draco, describes the windsock tail, or shows a Dacian national flag; Wikipedia's article is silent on the draco.

era-1991.says: Wikipedia says the RSFSR Supreme Soviet declared the imperial tricolour the national flag on 22 August 1991, that Decree No. 2126 of 11 December 1993 defined it as three horizontal bands with a 2:3 ratio, and that a federal constitutional law of 25 December 2000 legalised it. FOTW says the flag was raised over the Supreme Soviet building on 21 August 1991 and officially acknowledged on 22 August, that it was used alongside the Soviet flag until a December 1991 decree, that decree No. 2126 changed the ratio from 1:2 to 2:3, and that Flag Day was introduced on 22 August 1994.
era-1991.open: FOTW's contributors place the 1991 adoption steps differently (21 or 22 August). This page used to say the tricolour was the national flag from 1883 to 1917; the sources say it was authorised on land in 1883 and made the sole national flag in 1896.

FOTW says it was used as a naval ensign in 1693 without formal adoption, adopted as the merchant flag on 20 January 1705, became the civil ensign in 1799, and was recognised for use on land in 1883 as an alternate civil flag, Russia having two civil flags until 1914.
era-1721.open: FOTW and Wikipedia differ on 1693 (raised vs not formally adopted) and on 1883 (7 May or 28 April). This page used to say the tricolour became the official national flag by decree in 1883.

FOTW: Allard's 1695 flagbook shows a white-blue-red triband with a golden double-headed eagle, one with a blue saltire, and a red-and-white quartered flag with a blue cross.
era-1547.open: The sources show gold eagles on white or red grounds, not the black eagle on gold drawn here; neither mentions the 1497 seal or a gold or crimson tsar's standard, and neither covers 1547.
