era-1959.says: Wikipedia: on 4 April 1959 Senegal merged with French Sudan to form the Mali Federation, whose new green, yellow and red vertical tricolour bore a stylised kanaga figure on the centre band; on 20 August 1960 Senegal left, kept the colours and replaced the kanaga with a green star. FOTW: Mali Federation formed 4 April 1959, independence 20 June 1960, Senegal seceded 22 August 1960 (also given as 20 August) and replaced the 'kanaga (black man figure)' with a green star.
era-1959.open: Bambara and Dogon origin of the kanaga, and Mali's later retention of it, are not covered; FOTW and Wikipedia differ on the day (20 or 22 August 1960).

era-1659.says: Wikipedia: French authorities barred Senegal from using its own distinctive colonial flag (undated); a yellow star on green was used by the Republic of Senegal in 1958-1959. FOTW: no colonial flag described.
era-1659.open: The French tricolour over Saint-Louis and French West Africa, and the 1659 start, are not covered.

era-2006.says: Wikipedia says an Assembly recommendation of 2004 reintroduced the state and civil flags, the new constitution of 2006 sanctioned them, the Law on National Symbols was enacted in 2009 and the flags were standardised, with colour values, in 2010. FOTW says the Assembly declared Serbia the successor of Yugoslavia on 5 June 2006 and raised the state flag, that a 2009 law fixed 3:2 proportions with the lesser arms toward the hoist, and that the Government fixed the official designs on 11 November 2010.
era-2006.open: The flag's first return was 2004; 2006 is the constitution and independence.

era-279bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no state flag from Illyrian tribes, Roman Moesia, or the early medieval Serbian principality».
era-279bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1992.says: Wikipedia's «Flag of Serbia and Montenegro» gives adoption in 1992 and relinquishment in 2006, within a year of this era's 1992 and 2006.
era-1992.open: Wikipedia is the only source whose dates were compared; no linked Flags of the World page confirmed them. The design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1882.says: Wikipedia says the Kingdom adopted a state flag with arms and a civil flag without in 1882.
era-1882.open: One source. The design of the arms (a red shield with a white cross and four Cyrillic C letters, centred on the blue band) is not described by it; Wikipedia's 1839 firman puts the arms on the blue band.

era-1878.says: Wikipedia says the four stars were removed in 1878 after the Congress of Berlin, without a citation, and that a firman of January 1839 set the flag with arms on the blue band and four six-pointed stars on the red band. FOTW says the Serbian tricolour dates from 1835 and is based on Russian colours.
era-1878.open: This page says the kingdom's arms were not added until 1882 and that the tricolour was plain from 1878; Wikipedia's 1839 flag already carries arms.

era-1804.says: Wikipedia says the Sretenje Constitution named the national colours on 15 February 1835 and was abolished in April 1835, a firman of December 1835 allowed a merchant tricolour of red, blue and white, and a firman of January 1839 set arms on the blue band and four six-pointed stars on the red band. FOTW says the tricolour dates from 1835.
era-1804.open: The Takovo flag of 1815 is not covered; Wikipedia marks it citation-needed. This page used to put the stars in the canton and to say they came from the 1835 constitution.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia says that in 1945–1947 there was a Serbian Partisan flag, that from 1947 to 1991 the Socialist Republic kept the tricolour with a red star, and that in 1992, after a referendum without the required majority, the star was removed by an Assembly recommendation.
era-1944.open: One source, and it does not describe the star's gold border.

era-1918.says: FOTW describes the Kingdom's flag as blue-white-red, in use before the law and formally introduced with the 1921 constitution and prescribed by Article 2 of the 1922 law; Wikipedia's «Flag of Yugoslavia» gives the 1922 law. Wikipedia's «Flag of Serbia» says Serbia's tricolour use ended with the creation of the Kingdom in 1918.
era-1918.open: This page's statement that the blue-white-red was «presented as a neutral flag for the whole kingdom» was not found in either source.

era-1166.says: Wikipedia says the 1339 Dulcert portolan chart shows a white flag with a red double-headed eagle, that Dubrovnik records in 1281 a red and blue flag (colour order unknown), and that Dušan adopted the four fire-steel emblem on his coronation in 1346.
era-1166.open: The drawing now shows the portolan's white field and red eagle; an earlier version drew a red field with a white eagle. The gold detail is not from the source, and whether this was a flag actually flown is not established.

era-1941.says: Neither Wikipedia nor FOTW covers the Nedic regime (1941-44) or Chetnik flags.
era-1941.open: The page's claims about Serbian Volunteer Corps flags and Chetnik black flags are not covered by the sources read; no flag for the period is established.

era-1459.says: Wikipedia: a 1281 Dubrovnik inventory lists a red-and-blue Serbian flag, and its Ottoman-era coverage begins with the 1835 colours; neither source covers 1459-1804 flags.
era-1459.open: The page's statements that no Serbian civic symbol existed and about the Patriarchate of Pec are not covered by the sources read.

era-1402.says: Wikipedia mentions a 1439 portolan chart by Gabriel de Vallseca showing a flag of Emperor Dusan, with no colour detail; it does not cover Lazarevic's arms or a Hungarian-vassal shield.
era-1402.open: FOTW's page does not cover the Despotate; the drawing and the shield claim are unconfirmed.

era-1371.says: Neither source covers Prince Lazar or the 1371-1402 period.
era-1371.open: The claims that no banner survives and that a red cross Lazarica banner is attested only in later legend are not covered by the sources read.

era-1346.says: Wikipedia: Dusan was crowned Emperor of the Serbs in 1346 and adopted the four fire-steel (tetragramme) motif later used in Serbian flags; the 1339 Dulcert chart shows Serbia as a white flag with a red double-headed eagle.
era-1346.open: FOTW does not cover the Empire. The page's Cyrillic S reading, its motto, the cross shield and the silver eagle on red are not in the sources read.

era-1996.says: Both sources give 1996, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 8 January 1996; Flags of the World dates it 18 June 1996.
era-1996.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1977.says: WP: after Mancham was overthrown by France-Albert René in 1977 a red, white and green flag with a wavy white stripe, based on the SPUP flag, was used for 19 years until 1996. FOTW: a green, white and red wavy flag replaced the 1976 flag after a year following the coup.
era-1977.open: Neither source mentions a palm tree or star or the page's colour meanings. WP is inconsistent on the colours' attribution (SPUP vs United Seychelles).

era-1976.says: WP: independence flag (29 June 1976) with alternating blue and red triangles, used 1976-77. FOTW: white saltire dividing blue (hoist/fly) and red (top/bottom) fields.
era-1976.open: The page's green-white-red banded flag with shield is not supported by either source; meanings of colours not given.

era-1756.open: French royal ensign and Tricolor over Seychelles not covered.

era-1946.says: Wikipedia: own Crown Colony flag (one crown), captions 1946-1952 and 1952-1959, 1959 flag adopted 3 December 1959. FOTW: Union Jack flew 1819-1959; 1959 flag adopted 3 December 1959, designed by a committee under Toh Chin Chye.

era-1819.says: Wikipedia: Singapore was part of the Straits Settlements, flag a Blue Ensign with a red diamond and three gold crowns; the city had no separate flag. FOTW: the Union Jack flew over Singapore for 140 years (1819-1959).
era-1819.open: The two sources describe different flags for the span; the 1819 start and the Straits Settlements dates (1826 onward on the Malaysia source) are not reconciled.

era-1993.says: Wikipedia says the flag was adopted on 1 March 1990 as the flag of the Slovak Republic within Czechoslovakia, initially without the arms, that the constitution of 3 September 1992 added the coat of arms on the hoist side, and that a law of February 1993 described the details. FOTW says Slovak legislation of 1 March 1990 laid down the plain tricolour, that the constitution was enacted on 1 September 1992 with the flag in article 9, paragraph 2, that the flag was first hoisted on 3 September 1992 in front of Bratislava Castle, that the arms were added because the plain flag could be mistaken for Russia's, and that a law of 18 February 1993 set the shield's proportions.
era-1993.open: The sources differ on 1 or 3 September 1992 and on the article number. This page used to say the arms were first codified in 1939.

era-1990.says: Both sources say a Slovak flag, the plain white-blue-red tricolour, was adopted on 1 March 1990 within Czechoslovakia (Wikipedia: the interior ministry tasked Čisárik and Vrtel with the design). FOTW (Heimer) adds that the state flag was unchanged by that legislation.
era-1990.open: This page shows the Czechoslovak flag for 1990–93 and does not mention the Slovak flag of 1 March 1990. The «hyphen war» was not covered by either source.

era-1939.says: FOTW (Kravcik) says a law of 23 June 1939 enacted the white-blue-red tricolour as the Slovak State's flag. Wikipedia says the Slovak Republic used the flag during the war and that a war flag existed for its military.
era-1939.open: This page used to say the arms were added to the flag in 1939; neither source says so, and FOTW says they were added by the 1992 constitution. The 1939 constitution was not covered.

era-1938.says: Wikipedia lists, in an image caption, an official flag for the Autonomous Slovak Land within the Second Czechoslovak Republic in 1938–1939, and says the tricolour's current form dates back to 1848.
era-1938.open: One source, and it does not describe the flag. FOTW dates the first Slovak white-red bicolour to 23 April 1848 at Brezová, blue added in August 1848, and the present stripe order to after 1868 (Kravcik).

era-1918.says: FOTW (Sache) says the white-red flag was first officially hoisted in Washington on 18 October 1918, and Wikipedia says the National Assembly approved the flag with a blue hoist triangle on 30 March 1920 to distinguish it from Poland's.
era-1918.open: These sources are about the Czechoslovak flag, not Slovakia specifically; neither says the blue was chosen to include Slovakia (FOTW: the third Slavic colour from 1848; a Slovak-mountains reading is «late mythology»).

era-1699.says: For the Kingdom of Hungary, Wikipedia says red-white-green colours were visible at a coronation in 1790, formally described in 1806 and mandated by Act XXI of 1848; FOTW records the official colours in 1806.
era-1699.open: Neither source speaks of Slovakia or of the tricolour before 1790; this page's account of a single flag flown across the whole kingdom since 1699 is not confirmed.

era-1000.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Hungary) says the Árpád stripes were a dynasty standard in the 13th century and red-white-green cords appear on seals from 1323.
era-1000.open: About Hungary as a whole; nothing was found specific to Slovak-inhabited counties.

era-1948.says: Wikipedia: Czechoslovakia used its own flag 1920-1939 and 1945-1992. Flags of the World: Czechoslovak flag adopted 30 March 1920, blue triangle for Slovakia; communist period not covered.
era-1948.open: Flags of the World is silent on 1948-90; no source read states that no Communist symbol was added.

era-1945.says: Wikipedia: Czechoslovak flag used 1945-1992 and by the 1939-45 government in exile. Flags of the World: law of 23 June 1939 enacted the Slovak tricolor; 1945-48 not covered.
era-1945.open: The 1945-48 restoration is not described by either source.

era-1526.says: Neither source covers Hungarian flags for 1526-1699.
era-1526.open: Royal Hungary's flag and Slovakia's place in it are uncovered.

era-1991.says: Both sources give 1991, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 25 June 1991; Flags of the World dates it 27 June 1991.
era-1991.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-200bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1945.says: FOTW (Heimer, 1996) describes a white-blue-red flag with a star, officially adopted on 18 January 1947. Wikipedia says a red star was officially placed on the republic's flag in 1945.
era-1945.open: The dates differ: 1945 (Wikipedia) and 1947 (FOTW) for the start; FOTW gives the flag's abandonment as 27 June 1990, Wikipedia the removal of the star and adoption of the new flag as 27 June 1991. This page says 1945–1991. Neither source mentions the gold border on the star that this page describes.

era-1941.says: Wikipedia says the Partisans and the Slovene Home Guard both used Slovene national colours and that the Partisan flag, with a red star, was adopted on 26 September 1941. FOTW says the Home Guard, created by the German occupiers, used a Slovenian tricolour with the Carniola-derived arms, describes Partisan flags that are only vaguely like the postwar Yugoslav flag, and says it is not quite clear whether the Ljubljana Province arms were used as a flag before 1943.
era-1941.open: This page's statements that the German, Italian and Hungarian flags flew over their zones were not checked against a source. The caption says Slovenia «had none of its own»; the sources read describe Slovene flags in use, mostly by the Home Guard and the Partisans.

era-1918.says: FOTW describes the flag as blue-white-red, formally introduced with the 1921 constitution and prescribed by Article 2 of the 1922 law. Wikipedia's «Flag of Slovenia» says the whole kingdom officially used a blue-white-red flag while the Slovene tricolour stayed associated with Slovenia, and «Flag of Yugoslavia» gives the 1922 law.
era-1918.open: Wikipedia's infobox gives 1918 and its text 1922 for the flag's adoption. FOTW says the Slovene tricolour was soon banned or rarely tolerated under the kingdom.

era-29.says: Wikipedia gives the proclamation of the State as 29 October 1918 and its union with the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes as 1 December 1918 (Boban, 1993), and shows a flag image it does not describe. FOTW's Slovenia page says Slovenes adopted the tricolour when they joined the State in 1918 but that the State was too short-lived for the flag to be made official, and gives no colour order.
era-29.open: This page says red-white-blue. Neither source gives an order, so the order is unconfirmed.

era-1816.says: Wikipedia dates the Kingdom of Illyria from the patent of 3 August 1816 (citing Delo.si, 2006) to 8 December 1849, and shows a flag image without describing it.
era-1816.open: The white-over-red flag with an eagle described on this page is not confirmed by the source read.

era-1809.says: Wikipedia dates the Illyrian Provinces to 1809–1814/1815 and shows the French flag in its infobox, but describes no provincial flag.
era-1809.open: The page's statement about Slovene-language schooling and legal notices was not checked. Austria recovered the area in 1813–1814 according to Wikipedia.

era-973.says: FOTW says the white-blue-red tricolour was hoisted in Ljubljana on 7 April 1848, now Slovenia's flag day, and was used in 1848–1918 as the landesfarben of Carniola, which the Austrian rulers hardly recognised; it says Ferdinand I restored the Carniolan arms in 1836. Wikipedia says the tricolour was raised on 7 April 1848 by Lovro Toman and students and later recognised by Austria as Carniola's official flag.
era-973.open: The sources name different designers (Toman and students; Peter Kozler and Anton Globočnik). Wikipedia marks the 1836 date citation-needed, and FOTW's 1836 entry concerns the arms rather than the colours. Nothing was found for a Carniolan flag before 1848.

era-1849.says: Wikipedia: after 1848 the Austrian government recognised the white-blue-red tricolour as the official flag of Carniola, a regional exception (undated). FOTW: 1848-1918 the tricolour was Carniola's landesfarben, not a flag in the modern sense, and Austrian rulers hardly recognised it.
era-1849.open: The two sources disagree on recognition; neither describes a shared Habsburg black-and-gold banner over four crownlands.

era-1813.says: Neither Wikipedia nor FOTW covers the Austrian military restoration of 1813-1816.
era-1813.open: Not covered by the sources read; this is not a finding that no flag existed.

era-828.says: Neither Wikipedia nor FOTW covers the Frankish marches; FOTW dates Carniolan arms (Andechs red eagle) to the early 13th century, after this span.
era-828.open: The sources read are silent on flags or devices for 828-973.

era-658.says: Neither Wikipedia (Venice and Carantania appear only as navigation links) nor FOTW (Carantania not mentioned) covers Carantania or the black panther.
era-658.open: The claims that the panther is a later invention and was adopted by nationalists are not covered by the sources read.

era-1978.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1285.open: Wikipedia gives no design or evidence for these flags (they may be modern depictions); the page's statement that no flag survives is not confirmed either way. FOTW does not mention the sultanates.

era-1928.says: Wikipedia says the 1928 flag was first hoisted on 31 May 1928, based on the Prinsenvlag, with the Union Flag, the Orange Free State flag and the Transvaal Vierkleur in the white band; that the arrangement means each miniature flag enjoys equal precedence; that a brighter version was adopted in 1982; and that the flag was relinquished on 20 April 1994. FOTW says the old national flag was in use in 1928–1994, in blue, white, red and green.
era-1928.open: This page says the three small flags symbolise the union of Britain's and the two defeated Boer republics' domains; Wikipedia describes the arrangement as one of equal precedence. FOTW does not give the 1928 date.

era-1910.says: Wikipedia: four colonies formed the Union on 31 May 1910; the Red Ensign was the de facto national flag 1910-1928. FOTW: does not describe it.

era-1806.open: Cape Blue Ensign with badge, the Vierkleur and Orange Free State designs and any Natalia flag are not described.

era-1975.says: Wikipedia says an eagle change took effect on 21 January 1977, that Article 4.1 of the 1978 Constitution reads «The flag of Spain consists of three horizontal stripes: red, yellow and red», that Royal Decree 441/1981 of 27 February set the colours, and that the current arms date from 1981 (19 December in its text, 5 October in its infobox). FOTW says the Constitution was approved by Congress on 31 October 1978 and ratified on 6 December 1978, that Law 39 of 28 October 1981 allowed the arms on the yellow stripe, and that Royal Decree 2964/1981 (18 December, published 19 December) set the official arms and the flag's construction.
era-1975.open: The sources disagree on the 1981 arms date and on the act number. This page's «flown since 1785» is the naval ensign; the 1843 decree made it the national flag.

era-1939.says: Wikipedia says National Defence Junta Decree No. 77 of 29 August 1936 re-established the red and gold bicolour, that the Eagle of Saint John was added to the shield in 1938, that regulations of 26 July and 11 October 1945 fixed a bicolour with a new eagle in force until 1977. FOTW says a decree of 27 July 1938 set the State and war flag (it does not describe the design).

era-1936.says: Wikipedia says the National Defence Junta's Decree No. 77 of 29 August 1936 re-established the red and gold bicolour as the flag of Spain, and that the Eagle of Saint John was added in 1938.
era-1936.open: One source for 1936. This page's account of the Republic's flag is hedged because the stripe order is unconfirmed.

era-1931.says: Wikipedia says that on 14 April 1931 a tricolour of three equal stripes with a murrey (purple) third colour replaced the bicolour, reportedly to recognise Castile; it does not say which stripe is purple, calls it murrey in one place and indigo in another, and notes many authors say Castile's flag was crimson.
era-1931.open: One source, internally inconsistent. This page's stripe order and its Comuneros explanation were not confirmed, and the page text now says so.

era-1873.says: Wikipedia says that under the First Republic of 1873 the colours were unchanged but royal symbols were removed from the coat of arms.

era-1814.says: Wikipedia says a decree of 13 October 1843 from the government of Joaquín María López required Army, Navy and National Militia flags to use the war flag's colours, so that it was adopted by all the Armed Forces. FOTW says a Royal Decree of the same date made it the State and war flag and ensign.
era-1814.open: This page says the decree was under Isabella II, which is the reign; the sources attribute it to the government of the day. The era's claim about the Sexennium arms was not checked.

era-1808.says: Wikipedia says the red and yellow colours were used by the public and volunteers from 1808 and later became the colours of the Cortes of Cádiz and the National Militia; it does not mention Joseph Bonaparte.
era-1808.open: This page's account of a Bonapartist eagle was not found in the source, and the page text now says so.

era-1716.says: Wikipedia says a royal decree of 28 May 1785 set a red-yellow-red flag with a double-width yellow centre, to avoid confusion with other nations' flags «at long distances or with calm winds». FOTW says twelve war-ensign proposals were designed at the king's request and that a Royal Decree of 25 May 1785 set the war ensign.
era-1716.open: The decree date differs by three days (28 or 25 May 1785).

era-1516.says: Wikipedia says the Cross of Burgundy began to appear in Spanish flags from 1496, that Spanish armies used flags with it on different fields under Charles I (1516–1556), and, citation needed, that Philip II ordered each Tercio to carry a yellow flag with a red Cross of Burgundy.
era-1516.open: One source. This page's «white» field and its Mary-of-Burgundy account were not checked.

era-1874.says: Wikipedia: national flag listed as used 1874-1931 without a crown; crowned yacht ensign established 1875; flag origin 1785 decree of Charles III, yellow stripe double width.

era-1479.open: FOTW silent; no event for 1479 and the 'never merged' claim is contradicted.

Bandaranaike designed a gold lion on dark red with yellow border; two stripes (green, yellow/orange, each 1/7) added when Parliament adopted the flag on 2 March 1951 to represent Muslims and Tamils.

era-1814.says: Wikipedia says a common military ensign for Sweden and Norway, with a white saltire on red in the canton, was set on 6 June 1815, a common square-cut civil ensign in 1818, and that a royal resolution of 20 June 1844 introduced the union mark (the combined colours of both countries) on civil and naval ensigns; Norway adopted its own civil ensign in 1821.
era-1814.open: One source. This page describes the union mark as from 1844, which agrees, and as a combined red-white-blue emblem, which was not checked.

era-1523.says: Wikipedia says the oldest recorded pictures of a blue cloth with a yellow cross date from the early 1500s (citation needed), that the first legal description is a royal warrant of 19 April 1562, and that a warrant of 1569 required the yellow cross on battle standards and banners. FOTW, quoting a Swedish Institute leaflet, gives the same early-16th-century pictures, the 1569 warrant, reliable evidence on Swedish vessels from the 1620s under Gustav II Adolf, and the oldest existing flag warrant of 1663 (a triple-tailed flag, merchant ships square-cut).
era-1523.open: Neither source dates the flag to 1523. This page used to say the cross was the settled national banner throughout 1523–1814; the sources give 1562 and 1569 as the first legal steps and the 1620s as reliable evidence at sea. Wikipedia gives 1442 and 1448 for the arms that inspired it, inconsistently.

era-1397.says: Wikipedia does not cover a Kalmar Union flag; it says early post-Kalmar Union military flags used wavy stripes on blue.
era-1397.open: This page's «red-and-gold cross field with three crowns» was not found in the source read.

era-995.says: Wikipedia says the Three Crowns on blue appear since at least 1336 and that blue and yellow are said to have been Swedish colours since Magnus III's arms in 1275 (no citation).
era-995.open: Arms, not a flag. The page's mention of Magnus Eriksson's seals was not found in the source, and the earliest date given there is 1336, not 995.

era-1848.says: Wikipedia says a federal decree of 12 December 1889 set the cross arms at one-sixth longer than wide (7:6), that the Federal Act on the protection of arms of 2013 (in force 2017) defines the flag as a Swiss cross on a square background, and that the cross height was fixed at 5:8 in 2017. FOTW says Federal Order no. 111 of 12 December 1889 set the cross's relative dimensions with arms one sixth longer than wide, that Act no. 232.21 of 2013 defines the flag and colours, and that the margin was not officially fixed before 2017.
era-1848.open: The sources disagree on 1848: Wikipedia says the Federal Constitution did not name a national flag but prescribed the federal flag for federal troops, while FOTW says the flag was enshrined in the Constitution of 1848. This page says the 1889 decree fixed the proportions «for the first time»; FOTW says it replaced a five-square cross.

era-1815.says: Wikipedia says the Tagsatzung reintroduced the white cross on red for the federal seal, accepted on 4 July 1815, and that Bachmann's battalion flag of 12 October 1815 had a red square field and a white cross. FOTW says the restored Confederation adopted a seal with a short white cross and that honorary flags were given to returning regiments in 1815.
era-1815.open: Both sources describe the seal and army flags, not a national flag; Wikipedia says the Constitution of 1848 did not name one.

era-1798.says: Wikipedia: green, red and yellow tricolour imposed by the Helvetic Republic in 1798. FOTW: legion regiments carried flags bearing William Tell.
era-1798.open: The two sources describe different things; the tricolour layout is unconfirmed.

era-1291.says: Wikipedia says the first attested use of a white cross to identify Confederate troops was at Laupen in 1339, as two textile strips on clothing, and that at Arbedo about 1422 a triangular red flag with an elongated white cross was possibly the first flag used for the Confederacy rather than one canton. FOTW (Mills) says the Laupen troops wore a long-armed white linen cross stitched on breasts, sleeves and thighs, that at Arbedo in 1422 Confederate levies carried red triangular guidons with a white cross, and that the assumption that the flag derives from Schwyz's red banner is incorrect.
era-1291.open: The origin is unproven: FOTW mentions a derivation from a Holy Roman Empire banner, a tenuous Theban Legion link and a stitched-stripes theory. 1291 is the Confederacy's traditional founding, not a flag date.

era-1648.says: Wikipedia: white cross a field sign by the late 13th–early 14th century; Laupen 1339; Arbedo 1422 triangular banner; 1540 first mention of a separate Confederate flag. FOTW: 1339 white linen crosses; 1422 red triangular guidons with a white cross; 1540 last battlefield use; the Confederation was flagless in 1798.
era-1648.open: The 1648 recognition date is not in either source.

era-1803.says: Neither source covers the Act of Mediation or flags of 1803-1815 as such. Wikipedia: Bachmann used the white-on-red cross in 1800 and 1815; seal 4 July 1815, battalion flag 12 October 1815. Flags of the World: Confederation flagless before 1798, cross unused since 1540, honorary flags and armband in 1815.
era-1803.open: Cantonal flags and any 1803-1815 federal flag are uncovered; whether the cross was used in 1803-1814 is not stated.

era-1795.open: Neither source dates the 1795 start or calls the imperial flag a civil flag; Wikipedia's 1905 and 1917 flag displays show the page's 'none permitted' is too absolute.

era-1865.says: Wikipedia's table gives 36 stars in 1865–1867 (Nevada), 37 in 1867–1877 (Nebraska), 38 in 1877–1890 (Colorado), 43 in 1890–1891, 44 in 1891–1896 and 45 in 1896–1908 (Utah), the row data partly tagged citation-needed.
era-1865.open: One source. The page says 36 to 45 stars to 1912; Wikipedia's table puts 45 stars to 1908 and has the later 46-star flag, not described here.

era-1861.says: Wikipedia gives 34 stars in 1861–1863 (Kansas) and 35 in 1863–1865 (West Virginia), and says flag sales exploded after Fort Sumter.
era-1861.open: One source. This page's statement that the Union refused to remove any star is a comment, not a sourced fact.

era-1818.says: Wikipedia says Congress passed a plan on 4 April 1818, suggested by Samuel C. Reid, returning the stripes to 13 and setting 20 stars, with a star added for each new state on 4 July after its admission, and gives 33 stars in 1859–1861.
era-1818.open: One source; the statute's text was not read.

era-1795.says: Wikipedia says the stars and stripes were raised from 13 to 15 on 1 May 1795 for Vermont and Kentucky; it does not mention the Flag Act of 1794 (citation needed).

era-1777.says: Wikipedia says Congress resolved on 14 June 1777 that the flag be thirteen alternate red and white stripes with thirteen stars on a blue field, that the designer is unknown, and that William Canby first publicly told the Betsy Ross story in 1870 with no evidence in Washington's diaries or Congressional records. FOTW says Canby said he heard it from his grandmother and found nothing to support it in US records, that no record of a 1776 congressional committee on a flag exists, and that Francis Hopkinson was the only person at the time to claim credit.
era-1777.open: FOTW does not cover the 1777 resolution. The star arrangement is not specified by Congress, and the circular arrangement drawn is traditional, not documented.

era-1607.says: Wikipedia says the Continental Union Flag first appeared on 3 December 1775, flown by John Paul Jones aboard Alfred, and that whether the flag raised at Prospect Hill on 1 January 1776 was the Continental or the British Union Flag is disputed.

era-1610.open: Nothing on 1610-Victorian era; FOTW dated items begin 1904.

era-1299.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — Osman I's small frontier beylik, no fixed banner survives».
era-1299.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1922.says: Wikipedia: empire abolished 1922; caliphate standard of Abdulmejid II 19 Nov 1922 - 3 Mar 1924; Turkish Flag Law 29 May 1936. FOTW: Ottoman Empire ended 1 Nov 1922 when the sultanate title was eliminated; Republic proclaimed 29 Oct 1923.
era-1922.open: Pointer era; the sources do not describe the 1922-23 flag, and Wikipedia does not date the republic.

era-1844.says: Wikipedia: 1844 official adoption of the red flag with white crescent and five-pointed star (Tanzimat); eight-pointed star 1793-1844; a footnote dates the five-pointed star to Mahmud II (1826). FOTW: Zanamierowski dates 1793 introduction and 1844 five-point change without evidence; 1857 and 1905 charts show five-pointed star.
era-1844.open: Two sources give 1844 but FOTW flags its own source as unevidenced and Wikipedia has a rival 1826 claim.

era-1517.says: Wikipedia: Zulfiqar war flags common in the 16th-17th c.; star-and-crescent reported at Mohacs 1526 and Vienna 1683; 1613 naval flags (green with white crescent; white with red crescent); 1793 navy decree for a red star-and-crescent flag. FOTW silent on this period.
era-1517.open: Dates and sources of the plain red crescent banner for 1517-1844 are not established; FOTW silent.

era-1453.says: Wikipedia: simple crescent flag 'from its foundation in 1453'; Babinger on a possible Byzantine origin of the star and crescent; Selim I's Zulfiqar flag in the 1510s. FOTW silent.
era-1453.open: Red-field ancestry claim uncovered; FOTW silent on 1453-1517.

era-1362.says: Wikipedia: horse-tail tugh was the early military symbol; a 1721 source puts a crescent on infantry standards under Orhan (1324-1360). FOTW silent.
era-1362.open: Green battle standards for 1362-1453 are not stated by the sources read.

era-2700bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no attested banner; pre-vexillological ancient kingdom».
era-2700bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-633.says: Wikipedia: Arab-Muslim forces captured the derafsh after the Battle of al-Qadisiyyah (no year given). FOTW (pre-Islamic flags): Qadisiyyah dated A.D. 637 in one footnote and about 636 in another quoted source; the captured banner is given as about 22 by 15 feet.
era-633.open: Neither source states the Sasanian fall in 651 as a flag event; the Iran page cross-reference is not a source.

era-224.says: Wikipedia: the derafsh was the official standard of the Sasanian Empire (224-651), bejewelled, with a star emblem; the lead image is an artist's rendition. FOTW: Sasanian use is 'purported', later Sasanian coins do not show it, and no image survives so all depictions are reconstructions; Qadisiyyah dated 636 or 637.
era-224.open: The page's 636 date is one of two dates given by FOTW; the apron legend is from the Shahnameh (10th century) and its antiquity is not established.

era-247bce.says: Wikipedia: a scholar suggests the Parthian imperial standard 'seems to have been' the derafsh. FOTW: the flag-like device appears on coins of the Persis fratarakas (3rd-2nd centuries BCE) under Seleucid and Arsacid rule, vanishing by the end of the 2nd century BCE. Neither describes a horse-and-bow standard.
era-247bce.open: The Parthian bow-and-horse cavalry standard drawn here is not covered by any source read.

era-312bce.says: Wikipedia: Iranian coins of the 3rd and 2nd centuries BCE show the derafsh, including one of Baydad, a Persis governor under the Seleucids. FOTW: fratarakas' flag-like standard on coins under Seleucid and Parthian rule, possibly 'vexilloids'.
era-312bce.open: The Seleucid anchor device as a standard, and the 312 BCE start, are not covered by the sources read.

era-334bce.says: Neither source covers Alexander's conquest. Wikipedia (Faravahar): the symbol was not present in much Persian art after the Achaemenids. FOTW lists no Alexander-era flag.
era-334bce.open: The 330 BCE date and the claim of symbolic absorption are not covered.

era-550bce.says: Wikipedia (Faravahar): the winged-disc figure is on Persepolis reliefs and the tombs of Darius (r. 522-486 BC) and Artaxerxes III; derived from Assyrian winged-disc iconography (c. 865-850 BCE relief); meaning debated; not said to be a flag. Wikipedia (Derafsh): Xenophon says a golden eagle was the Achaemenid standard. FOTW: golden eagle on a white flag attributed to Cyrus (Herodotus, Xenophon, as quoted by Preble).
era-550bce.open: Whether the faravahar was ever a flag or royal emblem is not established; no verified image of a golden eagle standard; the drawing is a reconstruction.

era-753bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — the legendary Kingdom of Rome, no banner survives».
era-753bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1000bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — scattered Iron Age hut villages, no polity or banner yet».
era-1000bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1453.says: Neither source describes a flag for 1453; Wikipedia's Byzantine flags page mentions the fall of Constantinople only in navigation text.
era-1453.open: This is a pointer era, not a flag claim; the Ottoman flag of 1453 is handled on the Ottoman page.

era-330.says: Wikipedia: double-headed eagle not securely attested with the emperor before the 1301 chrysobull of Andronikos II Palaiologos (Soloviev: c. 1288); Pseudo-Kodinos (mid-14th c.) calls the tetragrammatic cross the customary imperial banner; bandon the main battle standard from the 6th c.; single-headed eagle on coins to 711-713. FOTW silent.
era-330.open: FOTW does not cover Byzantium; the page's 13th-century and aquila-descent wording is not matched by Wikipedia's 1301 attestation.

era-395.says: Wikipedia's Byzantine flags page does not cover Western Roman flags after 395 or 476 (it says vexillum and draco are still attested in the 5th century and beyond); FOTW silent on the division.
era-395.open: Flags of either half 395-476 are uncovered.

era-284.says: Wikipedia: Constantine's vision before the Milvian Bridge dated 27 Oct 312 (accounts of Lactantius and Eusebius differ); little evidence for the labarum before c. 317; Eusebius describes a gold spear with a Chi-Rho wreath and hanging banner. Wikipedia's Vexillum says Constantine replaced the spear point with the Chi-Rho. FOTW: the labarum bore the Greek X and P, undated.
era-284.open: Tetrarchy not covered; neither source says the labarum replaced pagan standards; the drawing's reconstruction status is not stated by the sources.

era-27bce.says: Wikipedia (Aquila): each legion carried one aquila; the Marius origin after 104 BC is Pliny's claim and disputed; bulls and wolves were also used by late Republican and early Imperial legions. FOTW: mentions an aquila only as a modern re-enactment piece.
era-27bce.open: SPQR on the aquila and the Principate-specific form are not covered.

era-509bce.says: Wikipedia (Vexillum): vexilla were cloth standards on a crossbar; SPQR on red Republic-era vexilla is 'sometimes reported' but unsourced, and one source finds no evidence of SPQR on army flags; sole surviving example (Pushkin Museum, 3rd c. AD) shows Victoria. FOTW: SPQR common in inscriptions but not known on flags in antiquity.
era-509bce.open: The SPQR-marked banner in the page's drawing is not supported; the Republic-period vexillum itself has no surviving example.

era-1187.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — rival gusuku lords and, later, three separate kingdoms, no shared banner».
era-1187.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1879.says: Wikipedia (Okinawa flag): the prefectural emblem became official on 15 May 1972 and the prefectural flag was adopted on 13 October 1972; under US rule only the US flag was permitted. Wikipedia (Ryukyu Kingdom): Okinawa Prefecture was established in 1879 (27 March in the body, 4 April in the infobox).
era-1879.open: Neither source says when the Japanese flag began to fly in Okinawa; Japan's flag for 1879-1945 is not covered, and 1945-72 is not what this page shows.

era-1872.says: Wikipedia: Emperor Meiji unilaterally declared the Ryukyu Domain (infobox: 16 October 1872) and appointed Sho Tai as domain head. FOTW does not cover the Ryukyu Han.
era-1872.open: No source read describes a flag for the domain; the Japanese flag shown and the 'legal fiction' remark are not covered.

era-1609.says: Wikipedia: the hidari mitsudomoe crest is called the first historical national symbol; Daisaku Kina (2012) found no contemporary source showing it used as a national flag, and ships bound for Satsuma after 1609 flew a banner with the Sho crest; a flag labelled 'flag of Ryukyu' from a ship drifting to Choshi in 1798 had a white field and black mitsudomoe. FOTW: no document or drawing of a national flag was found; a white flag with red, blue and yellow commas was probably invented after WWII; ship flags show the Sho three-comma emblem in both orientations.
era-1609.open: The sources do not say a flag was absent; they report none found. The red field shown here is not supported (sources describe white fields), so the drawing is a symbolic stand-in.

era-1429.says: Wikipedia: King Sho Toku adopted the hidari mitsudomoe in 1467 (a coffin inscribed with it and the year 1500 corroborates use); it does not describe any 1429 flag. Wikipedia and FOTW both report no document showing a national flag.
era-1429.open: The crest is dated after 1429 by the source, so it is not shown to be in use from the start of this era; the sources report no flag found rather than proving none existed.

era-1921-1.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — pre-republic era, no distinct territorial banner survives».
era-1921-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-200bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no unified banner from any of the successive steppe polities».
era-200bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia: absorbed 11 October 1944; the Tuvan Autonomous Oblast had no flag of its own (RSFSR flag shown 1944-1954); Tuvan ASSR from 1961 with flags from 1962; Republic of Tuva flag 17 September 1992, current design 2002. FOTW: 11 October 1944 absorption, local flags and arms abolished; ASSR flag 1961-1978 was the RSFSR flag with the Russian inscription, a Tuvan inscription added 10 November 1978.
era-1944.open: Whether the plain RSFSR flag was used 1944-1961 is not stated by FOTW; the page's Russian tricolour claim is not supported.

era-1943.says: Wikipedia: 8 September 1943 - 11 October 1944 flag with the initials in Cyrillic, a possible hammer-and-sickle variant. FOTW: 1941 constitution set a red flag with gold initials 'TAR' in the canton (1:2); in 1943 the initials became 'TAP' by custom rather than law; hammer and sickle not confirmed.
era-1943.open: The page's blue canton and hammer-and-sickle-style device are not supported; the drawing is not established.

era-1921.says: Wikipedia: independence proclaimed 14 August 1921; unofficial flag 1921-1926 known from reconstructions; first official flag 24 November 1926 - 18 October 1930 with 'Tuvan People's Republic' in Mongol script; 1930 flag red; 1941 and 1943 initials in Latin then Cyrillic. FOTW: plain red flags in 1921, 1926 constitution set a red flag with state arms in the centre; a blue flag with golden emblem for 1918-21 rests on one doubted source.
era-1921.open: The blue field with gold monogram canton is not supported; the page treats 1921-1943 as one flag but the sources describe several changes (1926, 1930, 1935, 1941).

era-1958.says: Wikipedia says the constitutions of 1946 and 1958 named the blue, white and red flag as the national emblem, quoting Article 2 of 1958: «the national emblem is the tricolour flag, blue, white, red»; that President Giscard d'Estaing introduced a lighter blue in 1974; and that on 13 July 2020 President Macron reverted the Élysée Palace to the darker hue without a statement. FOTW, citing the Société française de vexillologie, gives the same Article 2 wording for 1958, 1974 and 1976 for the lightening (Sache gives 1976), and 13 July 2020 for the darker blue, which it says was not officially announced and was mainly seen on state buildings.
era-1958.open: The sources date the lightening to 1974 or 1976. Neither names a shade, so the swatch colours are approximations. This is a start-year check only for the constitutional text; the flag itself dates from 1794.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia says the constitutions of 1946 and 1958 named the blue, white and red flag as the national emblem. FOTW's Third Republic page says a tricolour that had been the last flown in Paris in 1940 was raised again on 19 August 1944; its Fourth Republic page shows a flag image and describes no flag, and gives no dated adoption or change in these years.
era-1944.open: No source read describes the Provisional Government's flag. «PFG» in the FOTW account was not expanded by the source.

era-1940.says: FOTW says the French State kept the tricolour (Stilling and Müller), that its only new flag was the head of state's standard, prescribed by a decree of 19 March 1942 as a tricolour with seven gold stars on the white stripe below a francisque (du Payrat and Blanc), and that Free France had to add a charge to the tricolour because Vichy kept it, the cross of Lorraine being prescribed as its emblem by a regulation of 5 June 1941 (Sache). Wikipedia's captions say Pétain used a standard with a francisque in the white stripe and the Free French a cross of Lorraine in the white stripe, and its Free France article says Vice-Admiral Muselier created the naval jack with a red cross of Lorraine by general order no. 2 of 3 July 1940 and that d'Argenlieu suggested the cross.
era-1940.open: The sources differ on when the cross of Lorraine was adopted (June 1940 or July 1940 for the jack, 5 June 1941 for the regulation) and on who proposed it (Muselier, d'Argenlieu). Neither describes the cross-of-Lorraine flags in enough detail to draw, and the image shows the plain tricolour. The star colour on Pétain's standard is gold in the decree and blue in a 1941 scout book.

era-1870.says: Wikipedia says the Comte de Chambord demanded a white flag as a condition of accepting the throne, rejected it when offered the throne in 1870, and that the tricolour was kept. FOTW says Chambord insisted on the white flag with fleurs-de-lis in the dispute of 1873, that compromise ideas were a tricolour with fleurs-de-lis or a white flag with a tricolour cravat, and that he held out.
era-1870.open: The sources differ on the year of the dispute (1870 or 1873). Neither gives a law fixing the flag under the Third Republic.

era-1852.says: FOTW says Louis-Napoléon was proclaimed Emperor as Napoléon III on 2 December 1852 and that the national flag was the blue-white-red tricolour; the main France page says a regulation of 17 May 1853 officialised the 30:33:37 optical proportions for the ensign and that the dark navy blue was firmly established at least from the Second Empire.
era-1852.open: Both are Flags of the World pages, so this is one publisher; Wikipedia's article does not cover the Second Empire.

era-1848.says: Wikipedia says the Second Republic adopted a tricolour variant for a few days, 24 February to 5 March 1848, and captions Philippoteaux's painting as depicting the rejection of the red flag in front of the city hall. FOTW says a decree of 7 March 1848 confirmed the tricolour ensign.
era-1848.open: Wikipedia does not describe the variant. The painting is cited as depicting Lamartine, not as a document.

era-1830.says: Wikipedia says Louis-Philippe restored the tricolour in 1830 and that it has been used since except in 1848. FOTW says the tricolour had been banned since 1815, reappeared during the July days of 1830, that on 30 July Lafayette gave Louis-Philippe a tricolour on the city hall balcony, that on 1 August 1830 his ordinance stated that the French nation resumes its colours, and that he used a fleur-de-lis coat of arms from 13 August 1830 to 16 February 1831 before dropping it.
era-1830.open: FOTW's July Monarchy page does not cover the cockade, military flags with the Gallic cock or 1848.

era-1814.says: FOTW says the white flag was restored as the national flag in 1814, which it had not been under the Ancien Régime (Sache). Wikipedia says the tricolour was replaced by the pre-revolutionary white naval flag in 1815–1830. FOTW says that on landing from Elba in 1815 Napoléon had the tricolour hoisted, that a decree of 9 March 1815 ordered the tricolour displayed on town halls, and that the Hundred Days ended at Waterloo on 18 June 1815.
era-1814.open: The sources differ on 1814 or 1815 for the white flag. FOTW's Restoration page gives no decree and does not cover the white cockade or royal standards. This page draws the plain white flag, without arms.

era-1804.says: FOTW says Napoléon was proclaimed Emperor on 2 December 1804, that the national flag during the First Empire was the blue-white-red tricolour (Sache), that the bee served as an imperial symbol from 1804 to 1814 and in the Hundred Days, and that Napoléon had no personal standard before Elba.
era-1804.open: One source; Wikipedia's Flag of France article does not cover the Empire, and FOTW gives no decree confirming the flag.

era-1789.says: Wikipedia says the cockade was adopted in July 1789, Paris militia wearing blue and red with white added, that it became part of the National Guard uniform on 27 July 1789, that the Constituent Assembly approved a vertical red-white-blue tricolour on 24 October 1790, and that a resolution of 15 February 1794 reversed the order to blue-white-red. FOTW says the cockade existed by 12 July 1789, that the navy's jack and ensign of 1790 were the first vertical tricolours with red at the hoist, that a decree of 24 October 1790 became law on 31 October, that a decree of 26 June 1793 ordered tricolour flags on Paris public buildings, and that the decree of 15 February 1794 (27 Pluviôse, Year II) set blue at the hoist.
era-1789.open: Wikipedia says the attribution of the white is disputed, and FOTW calls the story of the king pinning the cockade a legend. The 1790 decree was about the flag generally, not only ships. The drawing shows the 1794 order.

era-1589.says: Wikipedia says the House of Bourbon ruled France in 1589–1792 and 1815–1848 and that the white Bourbon banner was used (image caption). FOTW says white was the royal and military colour, that the King's vessels carried plain white flags (Gay), and that a decree of 3 March 1781 prescribed the white flag on French consulates in the Levant, the first reported use of a white flag on land.
era-1589.open: FOTW says the white flag was a command flag and was not the national flag until 1814. Neither source describes a specific Bourbon royal standard.

era-987.says: Wikipedia says the red oriflamme, the banner of Saint Denis, was the royal banner under the Capetians; that the Valois arms of 1328 were blue with gold fleurs-de-lis bordered in red; that Charles V reduced the lilies to three about 1376; and that the blue field became the common standard of French armies in the Hundred Years' War. FOTW says the lilies first appear on Louis VIII's seal and on Philip II's banners (Gay), that Charles V reduced them to three in 1365, that a blue pendon with three gold fleurs-de-lis is described in 1350, and that in 1422 Charles VII adopted a white flag as his banner.
era-987.open: The date of the reduction to three lilies differs (1365 or about 1376). The oriflamme, which Wikipedia says was the royal banner under the Capetians, is not drawn, and the image shows the later blue banner for the whole span.

era-481.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — no flag documented for the Frankish kingdoms».
era-481.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-58bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — no flag documented for Gaul».
era-58bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1898.says: Both: a Royal Decree of 13 October 1843 made the red-yellow-red flag the State and war flag and ensign (Wikipedia: naval ensign from 1785). Neither covers 1898 itself.
era-1898.open: The sources read do not describe the Cross of Burgundy as Spain's ensign in 1898; they point to the red-yellow-red flag. The page's claim is contradicted and not replaced.

era-1808.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Spain): from 1808 the red-yellow flag spread among the people and volunteer units and was made official as the colours of the Cortes de Cadiz and the National Militia, undated. Cross of Burgundy article: flags with Ferdinand VII's crest were used in the Peninsular War and the Spanish American independence wars; the viceregal banner of New Spain lasted to 24 August 1821.
era-1808.open: FOTW is silent for this period; the page's 'royal red-and-gold' wording and the 1830s are not covered.

era-1580.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Spain): mid-16th-century companies carried their commander's arms over the Cross of Burgundy; in 1700 flags fell into a crimson royal standard, a white military flag with the cross and arms, and a white navy pavilion with arms. Cross of Burgundy article: under Philip V (1700-46) the naval ensign was white with the royal arms and the cross a jack; the red-yellow-red ensign replaced it by 1785.
era-1580.open: The page called the cross the naval ensign for this whole era and added a gold medallion; the sources read do not support that. FOTW does not cover the Habsburg or early Bourbon flags.

era-1535.says: Wikipedia: the cross served as the flag of the viceroyalties, with no dates given; the viceregal banner of New Spain lasted until 24 August 1821.
era-1535.open: FOTW and Wikipedia's Flag of Spain do not cover the viceroyalties; the 1535/1542 dates and 'naval and military ensign' wording are not in the sources read.

era-1519.says: Wikipedia: under Charles I (1516-56) Spanish armies used flags bearing the Cross of Burgundy on different fields, the official field staying white; the Cross of Burgundy article dates earliest Spanish use to 1506, the Flag of Spain article to after the 1496 marriage of Philip and Joanna.
era-1519.open: Neither names Cortes or Pizarro, so the link to the conquest expeditions is unconfirmed; FOTW is silent.

era-1492.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Spain): a pennant of the Catholic Monarchs, used until 1492 (file name 1475-1492); the text says Aragonese and Castilian flags and arms merged in 1475 (tagged 'citation needed'); the Cross of Burgundy only arrives after 1496.
era-1492.open: FOTW does not cover 1492; the design and 'reconstruction' status are not described in the sources read.

era-30bce.says: Neither source mentions the Roman annexation or any flag for it; Wikipedia's History of flags says nothing dated for Egypt.

era-305bce.says: Wikipedia (History of flags) says only that Egyptian bas-reliefs such as the Narmer Palette show early standards, that nome standards were 'vexilloids' of pre-dynastic Egypt, and that Diodorus describes sacred-animal standards; it names no period or dynasty and does not call them flags outright. FOTW's Egypt page covers no ancient period.
era-305bce.open: The Ptolemaic diadem, eagle and thunderbolt device and their use on standards are not covered.

FOTW's Egypt page covers no ancient period.
era-664bce.open: The Pschent as the Late Period emblem and the red-field reconstruction are not covered.

FOTW's Egypt page covers no ancient period.
era-1077bce.open: Competing dynasties and pharaonic symbols in this period are not covered.

era-1550bce.open: The uraeus and sun-disk as New Kingdom royal devices are not covered.

FOTW's Egypt page covers no ancient period.
era-2055bce.open: The Pschent as a Middle Kingdom emblem is not covered.

era-2181bce.says: Wikipedia (History of flags) says only that Egyptian bas-reliefs such as the Narmer Palette show early standards, that nome standards were 'vexilloids' of pre-dynastic Egypt, and that Diodorus describes sacred-animal standards; it names no period or dynasty and does not call them flags outright. FOTW's Egypt page covers no ancient period.
era-2181bce.open: Nomarch rule and the lack of a royal emblem are not covered.

era-2686bce.says: Wikipedia (History of flags) says only that Egyptian bas-reliefs such as the Narmer Palette show early standards, that nome standards were 'vexilloids' of pre-dynastic Egypt, and that Diodorus describes sacred-animal standards; it names no period or dynasty and does not call them flags outright. FOTW's Egypt page covers no ancient period.
era-2686bce.open: The Horus-name serekh and the Hedjet as Old Kingdom devices are not covered.

era-3100bce.says: Wikipedia (History of flags) says the Narmer Palette is said to be the earliest representation of standards and that nome standards were pre-dynastic vexilloids, without dating the palette; it does not mention the serekh. FOTW's Egypt page covers no ancient period.
era-3100bce.open: The serekh as the earliest royal identifying emblem and its Narmer connection are not covered by these sources.

era-1975.says: Wikipedia: the kingdom's flag lost official status 1975; government banner is the state emblem on white. FOTW: Sikkim became India's 22nd state in 1975; no official state flag; SDF flag de facto.
era-1975.open: Neither source says India's tricolour is Sikkim's state flag; that claim is uncovered.

era-1947.says: Wikipedia: khorlo with gankyil on every flag 1877-1975, simpler 1967 design with red border. FOTW: c.1914-1962 white field, triple border, red emblem; 1962-67 red wheel with six motifs.
era-1947.open: Neither describes a maroon field or crossed dorje; protectorate dates not given; the two sources' details differ.

era-1861.says: Wikipedia: first Sikkimese flag adopted 1877, images are reconstructions. FOTW: 1877-c.1914 flag 2:3, design not described; c.1914-62 white with triple border and red emblem.
era-1861.open: Maroon-and-gold banner, 1861 start and British protectorate dates are not covered.

era-1642.says: Wikipedia: Nepalese, Bhutanese and Tibetan banners until 1816, Union Jack to 1877, first Sikkimese flag 1877.
era-1642.open: FOTW gives no Namgyal flag; no source read supports the maroon-and-gold dorje banner.
